**[PINNACLE CONSUMER BRANDS, INC.]{.underline}**

**[SUMMARY OF INCENTIVE-BASED COMPENSATION CLAWBACK POLICY]{.underline}**

**Adopted by the Board of Directors on November 15, 2023**

**Prepared by Ashford & Sterling LLP**

**CONFIDENTIAL**

**Company:** Pinnacle Consumer Brands, Inc., a Delaware corporation **NYSE Ticker:** PCBI **Principal Offices:** 4200 Tryon Ridge Parkway, Suite 1100, Charlotte, NC 28217

This document is a summary of the Pinnacle Consumer Brands, Inc. Incentive-Based Compensation Clawback Policy (the \"Policy\"). The complete Policy text is on file with the Office of the Corporate Secretary and has been filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission as an exhibit to the Company\'s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023. In the event of any discrepancy between this summary and the full Policy text, the full Policy text shall govern.

**[Section 1 --- Purpose and Background]{.underline}**

Pinnacle Consumer Brands, Inc. (the \"Company\") adopted its Incentive-Based Compensation Clawback Policy (the \"Policy\") effective November 15, 2023, in compliance with Section 10D of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, as added by Section 954 of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act (the \"Dodd-Frank Act\"), Rule 10D-1 promulgated thereunder by the Securities and Exchange Commission (\"SEC\"), and Section 303A.14 of the NYSE Listed Company Manual. The NYSE listing standards require all listed companies to adopt and comply with a written clawback policy as a condition of continued listing. The Company\'s listing on the NYSE under ticker symbol \"PCBI\" requires strict compliance with these standards.

The Policy was prepared by the Company\'s corporate and securities counsel, Ashford & Sterling LLP, and was approved by the Board of Directors upon the recommendation of the Compensation Committee, chaired by Dr. Priya Nandakumar. Greystone Compensation Advisors, the Company\'s independent compensation consultant, was consulted during the policy development process.

The Policy supplements, and does not replace, any other clawback, recoupment, or forfeiture provisions contained in individual employment agreements, equity award agreements, or the Company\'s incentive compensation plans. The Policy applies to **all current and future Section 16 officers** of the Company. As a mandatory compliance matter, all executive employment agreements must contain an express acknowledgment of, and agreement to be bound by, the Policy. The Company\'s executive compensation playbook (last updated July 2025) requires that every executive employment agreement for a Section 16 officer include a Dodd-Frank clawback acknowledgment provision.

**[Section 2 --- Covered Executives]{.underline}**

\"Covered Executives\" under the Policy are all current and former \"Executive Officers\" of the Company, as defined under Rule 10D-1, which incorporates the definition of \"officer\" under Section 16 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and Rule 16a-1(f) promulgated thereunder. This includes the Company\'s president, principal financial officer, principal accounting officer, and any vice president in charge of a principal business unit, division, or function, or any other officer who performs a policy-making function.

The following positions are currently designated as Covered Executive positions at the Company:

> • Chief Executive Officer (Gerald Whitmore)
>
> • Chief Operating Officer (currently vacant; to be filled upon hiring)
>
> • Chief Financial Officer
>
> • General Counsel (Thomas \"TJ\" Jeffords)
>
> • Chief Human Resources Officer (Kendra Millstone)
>
> • Any other officer designated as a Section 16 reporting person by the Board of Directors

**Any individual who serves as Chief Operating Officer of Pinnacle Consumer Brands, Inc. is a Covered Executive under the Policy from their first date of service in such role.** The COO position is a Section 16 officer position, and any new hire into the COO role must acknowledge the Policy as a condition of employment and as a condition of receiving any Incentive-Based Compensation.

Coverage under the Policy extends for the three (3) completed fiscal years immediately preceding the date on which the Company is required to prepare an Accounting Restatement. Obligations under the Policy survive termination of employment with the Company for any reason.

**[Section 3 --- Incentive-Based Compensation Subject to Clawback]{.underline}**

\"Incentive-Based Compensation\" is defined consistently with Rule 10D-1 as any compensation that is granted, earned, or vested based wholly or in part upon the attainment of a \"Financial Reporting Measure.\" A Financial Reporting Measure is any measure that is determined and presented in accordance with the accounting principles used in preparing the Company\'s financial statements, any measure derived wholly or in part from such financial information, and stock price and total shareholder return (\"TSR\").

The following is an illustrative, non-exhaustive list of Incentive-Based Compensation subject to the Policy:

> • **Annual cash incentive bonuses** payable under the Company\'s Management Incentive Plan or any successor plan;
>
> • **Performance-based restricted stock units (\"PSUs\")** where vesting is contingent upon the attainment of financial performance metrics;
>
> • **Any portion of equity awards** where the grant, vesting, or payment is tied in whole or in part to a Financial Reporting Measure; and
>
> • **Any other compensation** tied to Financial Reporting Measures, as determined by the Compensation Committee.

The following forms of compensation are **not** Incentive-Based Compensation for purposes of the Policy: base salary, time-based restricted stock units (\"RSUs\") (to the extent vesting is solely service-based), signing bonuses, relocation benefits, discretionary bonuses not tied to Financial Reporting Measures, and benefits under broad-based employee plans.

Under the Company\'s standard executive compensation structure, the annual incentive bonus and PSUs constitute the primary forms of Incentive-Based Compensation subject to clawback. Time-based RSUs, which comprise approximately 40% of the standard annual long-term incentive grant (under the approved structure of 60% PSUs / 40% RSUs), would generally not be subject to the Policy unless their vesting is conditioned upon the attainment of a Financial Reporting Measure. For the avoidance of doubt, both the annual cash incentive bonus (target opportunity of \$525,000 for the COO position per the approved term sheet) and PSUs (target annual grant value of \$900,000 per the approved term sheet) constitute Incentive-Based Compensation subject to mandatory recoupment under the Policy.

**[Section 4 --- Triggering Events --- Accounting Restatements]{.underline}**

The Policy is triggered when the Company is required to prepare an \"Accounting Restatement,\" which is defined as: (a) a restatement of previously issued financial statements to correct an error that is material to the previously issued financial statements (commonly referred to as a \"Big R\" restatement), or (b) a restatement that corrects an error that is not material to the previously issued financial statements but would result in a material misstatement if the error were corrected in the current period or left uncorrected in the current period (commonly referred to as a \"little r\" restatement).

The applicable look-back period is the three (3) completed fiscal years immediately preceding the date on which the Company\'s Board of Directors, a committee thereof, or authorized officers of the Company conclude, or reasonably should have concluded, that the Company is required to prepare an Accounting Restatement. If the Company changes its fiscal year during a look-back period, the transition period resulting from such change shall be included in the look-back calculation in accordance with Rule 10D-1.

Recovery under the Policy is required **regardless of whether any Covered Executive engaged in misconduct or was at fault** in connection with the Accounting Restatement. The Policy imposes a \"no-fault\" mandatory recovery obligation. The Compensation Committee has no discretion to waive recovery except in the three narrow circumstances expressly permitted by Rule 10D-1, as described in Section 6 below.

**[Section 5 --- Calculation of Erroneously Awarded Compensation]{.underline}**

\"Erroneously Awarded Compensation\" is the amount of Incentive-Based Compensation received by a Covered Executive that exceeds the amount that would have been received had the compensation been determined based on the restated financial statements. For cash-based awards, this is calculated as the difference between the amount actually paid and the amount that would have been paid based on restated results. For equity-based awards where shares have been sold, the recoverable amount is the difference in value between what was received upon sale and what would have been received based on restated amounts. Where equity is still held, the Company may require return of shares or a cash equivalent based on the restated amounts.

For awards based on stock price or TSR, the Company must make a reasonable estimate of the effect of the Accounting Restatement on such measures, and such estimate must be documented and provided to the NYSE. There is no requirement to offset tax payments --- the gross amount of Erroneously Awarded Compensation is recoverable. The Compensation Committee will determine the methodology for calculating Erroneously Awarded Compensation consistent with the requirements of Rule 10D-1.

**[Section 6 --- Recovery Process and Limited Exceptions]{.underline}**

Upon the occurrence of a triggering Accounting Restatement, the Company will promptly seek recovery of all Erroneously Awarded Compensation from each affected Covered Executive. Recovery methods may include, without limitation: direct cash repayment by the Covered Executive, offset against future compensation payments, cancellation of unvested or unexercised equity awards, or any other lawful means determined by the Compensation Committee.

The Compensation Committee may determine not to pursue recovery only in the following three narrow circumstances expressly permitted under Rule 10D-1:

> 1\. The direct expense of enforcing recovery would exceed the amount to be recovered, provided the Company has first made a reasonable attempt to recover such amounts and has documented such attempt;
>
> 2\. Recovery would violate the home country law of a foreign private issuer that was adopted prior to November 28, 2022 (this exception is not applicable to Pinnacle Consumer Brands, Inc.); or
>
> 3\. Recovery would likely cause an otherwise tax-qualified broad-based retirement plan to fail to meet the requirements of Section 401(a)(13) or Section 411(a) of the Internal Revenue Code.

In all other cases, recovery is mandatory and the Compensation Committee has no discretion to waive or reduce the recovery obligation. The Company is **prohibited** from indemnifying any Covered Executive against the loss of Erroneously Awarded Compensation. The Company shall not pay or reimburse any Covered Executive for the repayment of clawed-back amounts, whether through directors\' and officers\' insurance, indemnification agreements, or otherwise.

**[Section 7 --- Acknowledgment and Compliance Requirements]{.underline}**

**Each Covered Executive is required to sign a standalone acknowledgment form** confirming that the executive has received, reviewed, and agrees to be bound by the Policy as a condition of receiving any Incentive-Based Compensation. The acknowledgment must be executed: (a) upon initial appointment to a Covered Executive position, and (b) upon any material amendment to the Policy. The form of acknowledgment is attached hereto as **Appendix A**.

In addition, **all employment agreements, offer letters, and equity award agreements** for Covered Executives must contain a provision expressly acknowledging the Policy and confirming that all Incentive-Based Compensation is subject to the terms of the Policy. The required contractual language, in substance, is as follows:

> *\"Executive acknowledges and agrees that all Incentive-Based Compensation (as defined in the Company\'s Incentive-Based Compensation Clawback Policy) received by Executive is subject to the terms and conditions of the Company\'s Incentive-Based Compensation Clawback Policy, as adopted by the Board of Directors effective November 15, 2023, and as may be amended from time to time (the \'Clawback Policy\'). In the event of any conflict between the terms of this Agreement and the Clawback Policy, the Clawback Policy shall govern. Executive agrees to promptly return any Erroneously Awarded Compensation as required by the Clawback Policy.\"*

The Company\'s General Counsel, Thomas \"TJ\" Jeffords, and the Chief Human Resources Officer, Kendra Millstone, are jointly responsible for ensuring that all new executive employment agreements contain the required clawback acknowledgment language. The Company\'s executive compensation playbook (last updated July 2025) mandates the inclusion of a Dodd-Frank clawback acknowledgment in all Section 16 officer agreements.

Failure to include the acknowledgment provision in an employment agreement does not relieve the Covered Executive of obligations under the Policy; however, as a matter of best practice and to avoid ambiguity or potential enforcement challenges, the acknowledgment language should always be included in the underlying agreement.

**[Section 8 --- Interaction with Other Recoupment Provisions]{.underline}**

The Policy is in addition to, and not in lieu of, any other recoupment, clawback, or forfeiture provisions that may apply to Covered Executives under: (a) individual employment agreements, including signing bonus clawback provisions and relocation clawback provisions; (b) the Company\'s equity incentive plans and individual award agreements; (c) the Company\'s Management Incentive Plan; (d) any other Company policy or plan; and (e) applicable law, including Section 304 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002.

In the event of a conflict between the Policy and any other applicable clawback or recoupment provision, the provision providing the greatest recovery to the Company shall apply. The clawback under this Policy is a \"no-fault\" mandatory recovery unrelated to individual misconduct, whereas other contractual clawback provisions may apply based on specified triggering events, such as termination for Cause or voluntary resignation, and serve distinct purposes.

**[Section 9 --- Administration, Amendment, and Governing Law]{.underline}**

The Policy is administered by the Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors, currently chaired by Dr. Priya Nandakumar, with authority delegated to the General Counsel for day-to-day implementation matters. The Board of Directors may amend or terminate the Policy at any time; provided, however, that no amendment or termination shall be effective to the extent it would cause the Company to violate Rule 10D-1 or applicable NYSE listing standards.

The Policy is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware with respect to corporate governance matters, and by federal securities law with respect to SEC compliance obligations. The Policy was filed as an exhibit to the Company\'s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2023.

Questions regarding the Policy or its application should be directed to the Office of the General Counsel, Thomas \"TJ\" Jeffords, at 4200 Tryon Ridge Parkway, Suite 1100, Charlotte, NC 28217.

There shall be **no guaranteed annual salary increases, cost-of-living adjustments, automatic escalators, or minimum increase floors** in any executive employment agreement. 90	
91	Signing bonuses may be offered to attract executive talent, particularly to offset compensation forfeited by the candidate at a prior employer, subject to Compensation Committee approval of the specific amount. The amount of any signing bonus shall be determined by the Committee based on documented evidence of the candidate\'s forfeited compensation (e.g., unvested equity, unpaid bonuses, or other compensation that will be forfeited upon departure from the prior employer). The CHRO shall present a memorandum to the Committee detailing the forfeited compensation and the proposed signing bonus amount.
92	
93	**Clawback Requirement (Mandatory).** All signing bonuses must include a **24-month pro-rata clawback** provision. The executive must repay a pro-rata portion of the signing bonus (calculated on a monthly basis over 24 months from the date of payment) if, within 24 months of payment:
94	
95	> \(a\) the executive **voluntarily resigns without Good Reason**, or
96	>
97	> \(b\) the executive\'s employment is terminated by the Company **for Cause**.

99	The clawback is calculated on a pro-rata basis as follows: the repayment amount equals the gross signing bonus amount multiplied by a fraction, the numerator of which is twenty-four (24) minus the number of full calendar months of employment completed after the date of payment, and the denominator of which is twenty-four (24). For example, if an executive receives a \$600,000 signing bonus and voluntarily resigns without Good Reason after 10 full months of employment, the executive must repay \$600,000 × (24 -- 10) / 24 = \$350,000.
100	
101	Signing bonuses are typically payable within 30 calendar days of the executive\'s start date, subject to applicable tax withholding. Payment may be structured as a single lump sum or, in limited circumstances, in two installments (50% on start date and 50% at six months), with Compensation Committee approval.
102	
103	No employment agreement shall limit the clawback to Cause-only terminations or shorten the 24-month clawback period. The clawback must apply to both voluntary resignation without Good Reason and Cause terminations. Signing bonuses exceeding \$500,000 require specific Board-level approval (not just Compensation Committee approval).

151	**[VI. SEVERANCE AND TERMINATION PROVISIONS]{.underline}**
152	
153	**VI.A --- General Principles**
154	
155	Severance payments and benefits are provided only upon a \"qualifying termination,\" which is defined as either: (1) termination of the executive\'s employment by the Company without Cause, or (2) resignation by the executive for Good Reason. The definitions of \"Cause\" and \"Good Reason\" are addressed in Sections VI.C and VI.D below.
156	
157	No severance is payable upon voluntary resignation without Good Reason, termination by the Company for Cause, death, or disability. In the event of death or disability, the executive (or the executive\'s estate or beneficiaries) is entitled to benefits under the Company\'s applicable benefit plans, life insurance policies, and disability insurance policies, which are separate from and not governed by this Playbook.
158	
159	**Release of Claims (Mandatory).** All severance payments and benefits are expressly conditioned on the executive\'s timely execution (and non-revocation) of a general release of claims in a form satisfactory to the Company (the \"Release\"). The Release shall be in a form prepared by the Company\'s General Counsel or outside counsel and shall release the Company, its affiliates, and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents, and successors from all claims, demands, and causes of action of any kind arising out of or relating to the executive\'s employment or termination thereof. The Release consideration and revocation period shall comply with the Older Workers Benefit Protection Act and shall be no less than 60 calendar days from the date of termination (inclusive of the 21-day or 45-day consideration period and the 7-day revocation period, as applicable). Severance payments shall not commence until the Release becomes effective and irrevocable.
160	
161	**Installment Payments Required.** Severance shall be paid in **substantially equal installments** over the applicable severance period on the Company\'s regular payroll schedule (currently bi-weekly). Lump-sum severance payments are **not permitted** except as specifically authorized by the Compensation Committee for Change in Control severance under Section VII.B, and only where such lump-sum payment is permissible under Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code. Installment payments preserve the Company\'s clawback rights in the event the executive violates restrictive covenants during the severance period and facilitate compliance with Section 409A.
162	
163	**VI.B --- Severance Amounts (Non-Change in Control)**
164	
165	The following maximum severance amounts apply to qualifying terminations that do not occur in connection with a Change in Control (for CIC severance, see Section VII.B):
166	
167	**Non-CEO C-Suite Officers (COO, CFO, GC, CHRO):**
168	
169	> • Cash severance: **18 months of base salary** plus **1x target annual bonus** (i.e., one times the executive\'s target bonus percentage multiplied by the executive\'s base salary as in effect immediately prior to the termination date).
170	>
171	> • COBRA: Company-paid COBRA continuation coverage for **18 months** following the termination date, or until the executive becomes eligible for comparable medical, dental, and vision coverage from a new employer, whichever is earlier.
172	
173	**CEO (for reference only):**
174	
175	> • Cash severance: 24 months of base salary plus 2x target annual bonus.
176	>
177	> • COBRA: Company-paid COBRA continuation coverage for 24 months.
178	
179	**SVP / Divisional President:**
180	
181	> • Cash severance: 12 months of base salary plus 1x target annual bonus.
182	>
183	> • COBRA: Company-paid COBRA continuation coverage for 12 months.
184	
185	Pro-rata bonus treatment on termination is addressed in Section IV above and is based on actual Company performance, not target or any other guaranteed amount. No additional payments, gross-ups, supplemental severance, or other compensation of any kind shall be payable upon a qualifying termination beyond the amounts specified in this Playbook.
186	
187	**VI.C --- Definition of \"Cause\"**
188	
189	The definition of \"Cause\" in every executive employment agreement shall include **all** of the following bases for termination:
190	
191	> \(i\) Conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony or any crime involving moral turpitude, dishonesty, or fraud;
192	>
193	> \(ii\) Willful embezzlement, misappropriation, or fraud against the Company or any of its affiliates;
194	>
195	> \(iii\) **Gross negligence or willful misconduct** in the performance of the executive\'s duties that causes or is reasonably likely to cause material harm to the Company or its reputation;
196	>
197	> \(iv\) **Material breach of fiduciary duty** owed to the Company or its stockholders, including the duty of loyalty and the duty of care;
198	>
199	> \(v\) Material breach of the employment agreement, including any restrictive covenant set forth therein or in any ancillary agreement;
200	>
201	> \(vi\) **Material violation of the Company\'s Code of Business Conduct and Ethics or any other material Company policy**, including but not limited to policies relating to harassment, discrimination, insider trading, and anti-corruption compliance;
202	>
203	> \(vii\) **Willful refusal to perform lawful duties** as reasonably directed by the Board or the executive\'s direct supervisor, after written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure (not to exceed 30 calendar days); and
204	>
205	> \(viii\) **Any act of dishonesty, fraud, or misrepresentation** that causes or is reasonably likely to cause material harm to the Company or its reputation, whether or not such act rises to the level of a criminal offense.
206	
207	**Cure Periods.** A cure period of 30 calendar days from written notice is appropriate for breaches that are reasonably capable of cure, specifically items (v), (vi), and (vii) above. No cure period is required for items (i), (ii), (iii), (iv), or (viii), as the conduct described in those provisions is of a nature that does not admit of cure or where immediate termination is warranted.
208	
209	**Overly Narrow Definitions Prohibited.** The definition of Cause shall not be limited to only felony conviction and embezzlement. An overly narrow Cause definition exposes the Company to significant severance liability by making it effectively impossible to terminate an underperforming or misbehaving executive for Cause, even where such executive has engaged in gross negligence, willful misconduct, policy violations, fiduciary duty breaches, or other serious misconduct that falls short of criminal conviction. Every element listed above serves a distinct and important protective function and must be included in each executive employment agreement. Outside counsel should push back firmly on any attempt by an executive\'s counsel to narrow the Cause definition below this standard.
210	
211	**VI.D --- Definition of \"Good Reason\"**
212	
213	The definition of \"Good Reason\" in every executive employment agreement shall be limited to the following standard triggers, each of which must occur without the executive\'s prior written consent:
214	
215	> \(i\) A **material diminution** in the executive\'s authority, duties, or responsibilities (excluding changes resulting from the Company ceasing to be a publicly traded entity or becoming a subsidiary of another entity following a Change in Control, provided such change does not otherwise materially diminish the executive\'s authority, duties, or responsibilities with respect to the surviving or acquiring entity\'s operations);
216	>
217	> \(ii\) A **material reduction** in the executive\'s base salary (other than an across-the-board reduction of not more than 10% applicable to all similarly situated executives);
218	>
219	> \(iii\) A **relocation** of the executive\'s principal place of employment by more than **50 miles** from the executive\'s then-current principal place of employment; and
220	>
221	> \(iv\) A **material breach** by the Company of the employment agreement that remains uncured after the notice and cure period specified below.
222	
223	**Notice and Cure.** The executive must provide written notice to the Company within 60 calendar days of the initial occurrence of the condition giving rise to Good Reason. The Company shall have 30 calendar days following receipt of such notice to cure the condition. If the Company cures the condition within the 30-day cure period, Good Reason shall be deemed not to have occurred with respect to such condition. If the Company does not cure the condition within the 30-day cure period, the executive must resign within 30 calendar days following the expiration of the cure period. Failure to resign within this 30-day window shall constitute a waiver of the Good Reason event.

225	**Prohibited Good Reason Triggers.** The following shall **not** be included as Good Reason triggers in any executive employment agreement:
226	
227	> • *Reduction in number of direct reports or changes to organizational reporting structure.* Organizational structure and reporting lines are management prerogatives subject to change based on business needs. The number of direct reports is not a material term of the executive\'s employment, and including such a trigger creates operational inflexibility.
228	>
229	> • *Office size, location within a building, or other physical workspace specifications.* These are operational matters addressed by the Company\'s standard executive office policy and are not appropriate subjects for contractual commitment.
230	>
231	> • *Failure to nominate or elect the executive to the Board of Directors.* Board nominations are the sole prerogative of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and the full Board. Contractual commitments regarding board seats improperly constrain the Board\'s fiduciary duties under the Delaware General Corporation Law and create potential conflicts of interest. See also Section X below.
232	>
233	> • *Open-ended \"catch-all\" provisions.* Language such as \"any other action that materially and adversely affects the Executive\'s status, working conditions, or compensation\" is unacceptably vague and effectively grants the executive de facto unilateral resignation-for-Good-Reason rights. Such provisions expose the Company to severance liability on the basis of subjective and inherently disputable claims.
234	>
235	> • *Target bonus reductions.* The target bonus percentage under the AIP is set annually by the Compensation Committee in its discretion. Including target bonus reduction as a Good Reason trigger inappropriately constrains the Committee\'s authority and is inconsistent with the discretionary nature of the AIP.
236	
237	The relocation distance threshold is 50 miles. A threshold of 25 miles is below market norms for publicly traded consumer products companies and should not be accepted. The 50-mile standard is consistent with the Company\'s peer group and with prevailing market practice.

239	**[VII. CHANGE IN CONTROL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**
240	
241	**VII.A --- Double-Trigger Requirement**
242	
243	All equity acceleration and Change in Control (\"CIC\") severance payments and benefits must be subject to a **\"double-trigger\"** mechanism. Under the double-trigger structure, the executive is entitled to CIC severance and equity acceleration only if both of the following conditions are satisfied:
244	
245	> \(1\) A Change in Control event occurs (as defined in the Equity Plan or, if different, in the employment agreement, provided the definition is consistent with the Equity Plan and Section 409A); **and**
246	>
247	> \(2\) The executive\'s employment is terminated by the Company (or its successor) without Cause, or the executive resigns for Good Reason, in each case within **24 months** following the consummation of the Change in Control.
248	
249	**Single-Trigger Acceleration Is Prohibited.** Equity shall not accelerate solely upon the occurrence of a Change in Control absent a qualifying termination of employment. Single-trigger acceleration creates perverse incentives, encouraging executives to depart the Company following a transaction rather than assisting with post-closing integration, and results in a windfall that is unrelated to the executive\'s continued performance and contribution. Single-trigger vesting is also disfavored by proxy advisory firms, including Institutional Shareholder Services (ISS) and Glass Lewis, and may result in negative say-on-pay voting recommendations. Any draft employment agreement that includes single-trigger acceleration must be revised to incorporate the double-trigger structure before execution.
250	
251	If a successor entity in a CIC transaction does not assume or substitute outstanding equity awards on substantially equivalent terms (as determined in good faith by the Compensation Committee), vesting of such equity awards shall accelerate upon the closing of the CIC transaction. This provision is not considered single-trigger acceleration because the failure to assume or substitute the awards creates a deemed qualifying event --- the executive\'s equity would otherwise be cancelled without adequate replacement, which is economically equivalent to a forfeiture.
252	
253	**VII.B --- CIC Severance Amounts**
254	
255	The following maximum CIC severance amounts apply to qualifying terminations occurring within 24 months following a Change in Control:
256	
257	**Non-CEO C-Suite Officers (COO, CFO, GC, CHRO):**
258	
259	> • Cash severance: **2x base salary** plus **2x target annual bonus**.
260	>
261	> • COBRA: Company-paid COBRA continuation coverage for **24 months**.
262	>
263	> • Full acceleration of all unvested equity awards (subject to the double-trigger requirement set forth in Section VII.A above).
264	
265	**CEO (for reference only):**
266	
267	> • Cash severance: 3x base salary plus 3x target annual bonus.
268	>
269	> • COBRA: 24 months.
270	>
271	> • Full equity acceleration (double-trigger).
272	
273	CIC severance is in lieu of (not in addition to) the non-CIC severance described in Section VI.B. In the event a qualifying termination occurs within 24 months following a Change in Control, the executive shall receive the greater of the CIC severance and the non-CIC severance, but not both. The agreement shall include language making clear that the CIC severance and non-CIC severance are mutually exclusive.
274	
275	CIC severance is subject to the same mandatory release of claims requirement and, as a default, the same installment payment structure as non-CIC severance (see Section VI.A), except that the Compensation Committee may approve lump-sum CIC severance payments on a case-by-case basis where Section 409A permits such payment (e.g., under the short-term deferral exception under Treasury Regulation § 1.409A-1(b)(4) or the involuntary separation pay safe harbor under Treasury Regulation § 1.409A-1(b)(9)(iii)).
276	
277	**VII.C --- Section 280G Treatment**
278	
279	**Best Net Cutback (Mandatory).** All executive employment agreements must include a **\"best net\" cutback** provision addressing the potential application of Sections 280G and 4999 of the Internal Revenue Code (the \"Code\"). Under this provision, if any payments or benefits to the executive in connection with a Change in Control would constitute \"parachute payments\" within the meaning of Section 280G of the Code, then such payments and benefits shall be reduced (but not below zero) to the maximum amount that would not trigger the excise tax imposed by Section 4999 of the Code, **but only if** the net after-tax benefit to the executive after such reduction (taking into account all applicable federal, state, and local income taxes and payroll taxes) exceeds the net after-tax benefit the executive would receive without such reduction (after accounting for the Section 4999 excise tax and all applicable income and payroll taxes).
280	
281	In other words, the executive receives whichever approach --- full payment with the excise tax or reduced payment without the excise tax --- results in the greater net after-tax benefit to the executive. This structure protects the Company from the cost and reputational harm of gross-up payments while ensuring the executive receives the economically optimal result.
282	
283	**Gross-Ups Prohibited.** Under no circumstances shall any executive employment agreement include a **Section 280G excise tax gross-up** provision. This prohibition is absolute and applies regardless of the executive\'s position, compensation level, negotiating leverage, or the competitive dynamics of the particular search. Gross-up provisions represent a significant and unpredictable cost to the Company, are strongly disfavored by proxy advisory firms (including ISS and Glass Lewis) and institutional investors, create negative optics in the Company\'s annual proxy statement, and may result in adverse say-on-pay voting recommendations. The Company has maintained a no-gross-up policy since the original adoption of this Playbook in March 2021, and no exceptions have been or will be granted.
284	
285	The Section 280G analysis should be performed by the Company\'s independent accounting firm or a qualified third-party tax advisor promptly following any Change in Control transaction (or, where practicable, prior to closing). The cost of such analysis shall be borne by the Company.
286	
287	The reduction methodology shall be specified in the employment agreement as follows: if a cutback is required, payments and benefits shall be reduced in the following order: (1) cash severance payments, (2) accelerated equity vesting, (3) any other parachute payments, in each case in reverse chronological order of payment (i.e., the payment furthest in time from the date of the Change in Control shall be reduced first).

296	
297	**Scope of Restricted Activity.** The non-compete shall prohibit the executive from directly or indirectly engaging in, being employed by, consulting for, or providing services to any business that is **competitive with any line of business** of the Company or its subsidiaries as conducted at any time during the 12 months preceding the date of termination. As of the date of this Playbook, the Company\'s business lines include:

299	> • Premium household cleaning products
300	>
301	> • Personal care items
302	>
303	> • Specialty food products
304	>
305	> • Pet care products (via Harmony Pet Naturals, Inc., acquired Q3 2024)

308	
309	**Geographic Scope.** The non-compete shall apply in **all geographic areas in which the Company or its subsidiaries conduct business** (currently 14 states domestically, plus international markets as applicable). The non-compete shall not be limited to a single metropolitan area or region.

311	**Consideration.** For at-hire agreements, the employment itself constitutes adequate consideration for the non-compete under North Carolina law. For existing employees entering into new or amended employment agreements containing non-compete provisions, continued employment is sufficient consideration. No additional \"garden leave\" compensation or separate consideration for the non-compete is required under applicable law.
312	
313	**Garden Leave Pay.** The Company **does not** provide garden leave compensation during the non-compete period. The non-compete consideration is embedded in the severance payments provided under Section VI (which are, in part, conditioned on the executive\'s compliance with restrictive covenants, including the non-compete). Any provision requiring the Company to pay the executive\'s full base salary, a percentage of base salary, or any other compensation during the restricted period as \"garden leave\" or \"non-compete consideration\" is **not permitted** and shall be struck from any draft agreement. North Carolina does not have a statutory garden-leave requirement, and the Company\'s standard practice --- consistent with the overwhelming majority of its peer group --- does not include garden leave pay.

435	**[XIII. TAX COMPLIANCE AND SECTION 409A]{.underline}**
436	
437	All executive employment agreements must include a comprehensive **Section 409A compliance provision** (commonly referred to as a \"409A savings clause\"). This is a mandatory requirement for all agreements that include deferred compensation elements, which encompasses virtually all executive employment agreements given the presence of severance, bonus, and equity provisions.
438	
439	**Key Section 409A Requirements:**
440	
441	> *General Compliance Provision.* The agreement must provide that all payments and benefits shall be interpreted and administered in a manner consistent with Section 409A of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (\"Section 409A\"), and the Treasury Regulations and other guidance promulgated thereunder. To the extent any provision of the agreement is ambiguous as to its compliance with Section 409A, the provision shall be read in such a manner so that all payments hereunder comply with Section 409A.
442	>
443	> *Specified Employee Six-Month Delay.* If the executive is a \"specified employee\" (as defined in Section 409A and Treasury Regulation § 1.409A-1(i)) at the time of a \"separation from service\" (as defined in Section 409A and Treasury Regulation § 1.409A-1(h)), any payments that constitute \"nonqualified deferred compensation\" subject to Section 409A shall not be paid until the date that is six months after the executive\'s separation from service (or, if earlier, the executive\'s date of death). Any payments that are delayed pursuant to this provision shall be accumulated without interest and paid in a lump sum on the first business day following the six-month anniversary of the separation from service. As a publicly traded company listed on the New York Stock Exchange, Pinnacle will have \"specified employees\" under Section 409A, and any C-suite executive compensated above the threshold specified in Section 416(i) of the Code (currently \$220,000 for 2025) will almost certainly qualify as a specified employee.
444	>
445	> *Separation from Service.* A termination of employment shall not be deemed to have occurred for purposes of Section 409A unless such termination constitutes a \"separation from service\" within the meaning of Treasury Regulation § 1.409A-1(h).
446	>
447	> *Separate Payments.* Each installment of severance or other payment shall be treated as a separate \"payment\" for purposes of Section 409A.
448	>
449	> *Exemptions.* To the extent permissible, payments should be structured to fall within the short-term deferral exception (Treasury Regulation § 1.409A-1(b)(4)) or the involuntary separation pay safe harbor (Treasury Regulation § 1.409A-1(b)(9)(iii)), thereby exempting such payments from Section 409A\'s requirements.
450	
451	**Omission of a Section 409A savings clause is a critical compliance failure.** The Company and the executive face potentially severe tax consequences if payments are made in violation of Section 409A, including a 20% additional federal income tax on the executive, plus interest at the underpayment rate plus one percentage point, calculated from the date the deferred compensation is or should have been includible in gross income. The Company may also face reputational risk, employee relations issues, and potential indemnification claims.
452	
453	Outside counsel at Redmond, Pace & Varela LLP should review all payment timing provisions in draft employment agreements for Section 409A compliance before execution. Any questions regarding the application of Section 409A to specific payment structures should be referred to the Company\'s tax advisors.

455	**[XIV. DODD-FRANK CLAWBACK ACKNOWLEDGMENT]{.underline}**
456	
457	All executive employment agreements for Section 16 officers must include an express **acknowledgment** that the executive\'s incentive-based compensation is subject to the Company\'s **Compensation Recovery Policy** (the \"Clawback Policy\"), adopted in November 2023 in compliance with Securities and Exchange Commission Rule 10D-1 and New York Stock Exchange Listed Company Manual Section 303A.14. The Clawback Policy was prepared by Ashford & Sterling LLP and has been filed with the SEC as an exhibit to the Company\'s most recent Annual Report on Form 10-K.
458	
459	The Clawback Policy requires the mandatory recovery of erroneously awarded incentive-based compensation received by current and former executive officers during the three completed fiscal years immediately preceding any required accounting restatement (including restatements to correct an error in previously issued financial statements that is material to the previously issued financial statements, or that would result in a material misstatement if the error were corrected in the current period or left uncorrected in the current period). Recovery is required regardless of fault, and the Compensation Committee does not have discretion to waive recovery except in the limited circumstances specified in the Clawback Policy and Rule 10D-1 (i.e., where recovery would be impracticable because the direct expense of enforcing recovery would exceed the amount to be recovered, recovery would violate applicable home country law, or recovery would likely cause a tax-qualified retirement plan to fail to meet applicable qualification requirements).
460	
461	The acknowledgment provision in the employment agreement shall state:
462	
463	> \"The Executive acknowledges and agrees that all incentive-based compensation (as defined in the Company\'s Compensation Recovery Policy adopted pursuant to SEC Rule 10D-1 and the applicable listing standards of the New York Stock Exchange) paid or granted to the Executive pursuant to this Agreement or otherwise is subject to the terms and conditions of the Company\'s Compensation Recovery Policy, as in effect from time to time. In the event of a conflict between this Agreement and the Compensation Recovery Policy, the Compensation Recovery Policy shall govern.\"
464	
465	Failure to include this acknowledgment in an executive employment agreement creates a potential compliance gap with NYSE listing standards and exposes the Company to risk in the event a clawback becomes necessary. The Clawback Policy is on file with the SEC and is available from the General Counsel\'s office upon request.
466	
467	This requirement applies to all forms of incentive compensation, including annual bonuses paid under the AIP, PSUs, RSUs, stock options (if applicable), and any other compensation that is granted, earned, or vested based wholly or in part on the attainment of financial reporting measures (as defined in Rule 10D-1).
468	
469	**[XV. DISPUTE RESOLUTION]{.underline}**
470	
471	**Binding Arbitration Required.** All disputes arising out of or relating to an executive employment agreement, or the breach, termination, enforcement, interpretation, or validity thereof, including the determination of the scope or applicability of the arbitration provision, shall be resolved through **binding arbitration** administered by the American Arbitration Association (\"AAA\") under its Employment Arbitration Rules and Mediation Procedures then in effect. The arbitration shall be conducted by a single arbitrator with experience in executive employment disputes, selected in accordance with the AAA\'s rules.
472	
473	**Venue.** The seat of arbitration shall be Charlotte, North Carolina (Mecklenburg County). For executives whose principal place of employment is the Company\'s Charlotte headquarters, the arbitration venue shall be Charlotte, NC. Litigation or arbitration in any other jurisdiction --- including the executive\'s prior state of residence, the state in which the executive relocates following termination, or any other location --- is not acceptable and must be rejected during negotiations.
474	
475	**Governing Law.** North Carolina law shall govern the employment agreement and all disputes arising thereunder for all Charlotte-based executives, without regard to conflict of laws principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. This choice of law provision is essential to ensure consistency and predictability in the enforcement of the Company\'s employment agreements, particularly with respect to restrictive covenant provisions.
476	
477	**Attorneys\' Fees.** Each party shall bear its own attorneys\' fees, costs, and expenses incurred in connection with any arbitration or other proceeding arising under the employment agreement. **One-sided fee-shifting provisions** --- such as \"the Company shall pay the Executive\'s reasonable attorneys\' fees and costs if the Executive substantially prevails on any material claim\" without a reciprocal obligation --- are **not acceptable**. Such provisions create asymmetric incentives, encourage frivolous or marginal claims, and impose potentially significant unbudgeted legal costs on the Company. Mutual prevailing-party fee-shifting provisions may be considered on a case-by-case basis with the prior approval of both the Compensation Committee and the General Counsel, but the default position is that each party bears its own fees.
478	
479	The arbitration provision shall include carve-outs permitting either party to seek emergency temporary restraining orders, preliminary injunctive relief, or other equitable relief in a court of competent jurisdiction (located in Charlotte, Mecklenburg County, North Carolina) to enforce restrictive covenants or protect Confidential Information, without waiving the right to compel arbitration of the underlying dispute. This carve-out is essential to ensure the Company can obtain prompt injunctive relief to prevent irreparable harm in the event of a restrictive covenant violation.
480	
481	The employment agreement shall also include class action and collective action waivers and a waiver of the right to a jury trial, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law.
482	
483	**[XVI. MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS]{.underline}**
484	
485	The following miscellaneous provisions should be included in all executive employment agreements in substantially the form described below. These provisions are standard and should not require significant negotiation.
486	
487	**Indemnification and D&O Insurance.** Executive officers are entitled to indemnification to the fullest extent permitted by the Delaware General Corporation Law and the Company\'s Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation and Amended and Restated Bylaws, as in effect from time to time. The Company shall maintain directors\' and officers\' liability insurance coverage at customary levels and shall include the executive as a covered insured under such policies. Indemnification provisions in employment agreements should reference the Company\'s standard form of Indemnification Agreement (a separate document executed concurrently with the employment agreement) rather than including bespoke indemnification terms in the body of the employment agreement. A copy of the standard Indemnification Agreement is available from the General Counsel\'s office.
488	
489	**Section 409A.** See Section XIII above. A comprehensive Section 409A savings clause is mandatory in all executive employment agreements and must be included without exception.
490	
491	**Clawback.** See Section XIV above. A Dodd-Frank Clawback Policy acknowledgment is mandatory for all Section 16 officers and must be included without exception.
492	
493	**Entire Agreement / Amendment.** The agreement shall contain a standard entire agreement clause providing that the agreement constitutes the entire agreement between the parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous agreements, representations, and understandings. The agreement may be amended only by a written instrument executed by both parties.
494	
495	**Severability.** The agreement shall contain a standard severability clause providing that if any provision is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, such provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid, legal, and enforceable, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect.
496	
497	**Counterparts.** The agreement may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument.
498	
499	**Notices.** A standard notice provision shall be included with the Company\'s address (4200 Tryon Ridge Parkway, Suite 1100, Charlotte, NC 28217, Attn: General Counsel) and the executive\'s address as set forth in the Company\'s records.
500	
501	**No Waiver.** The failure by either party to enforce any provision of the agreement shall not constitute a waiver of such provision or of the right to enforce such provision at a later time.
502	
503	**Withholding.** All payments and benefits under the agreement shall be subject to applicable federal, state, and local tax withholding requirements.
504	
505	**Assignment.** The Company may assign the agreement to any successor in connection with a merger, consolidation, reorganization, or sale of all or substantially all of the Company\'s assets. The executive may not assign the agreement or any rights or obligations thereunder without the prior written consent of the Company.
506

275	**Section 10.5 --- Cooperation.** Following any termination of the Executive\'s employment (regardless of the reason for such termination), the Executive shall reasonably cooperate with the Company in connection with any pending or future litigation, investigation, regulatory proceeding, audit, or other matter relating to events that occurred during the Executive\'s employment with the Company. The Company shall reimburse the Executive for all reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with such cooperation, and shall use reasonable efforts to schedule such cooperation at mutually convenient times so as not to unreasonably interfere with the Executive\'s other professional or personal obligations.
276	
277	**[SECTION 11 --- CHANGE IN CONTROL]{.underline}**
278	
279	**Section 11(a) --- Definition of Change in Control.** For purposes of this Agreement, a \"**Change in Control**\" shall mean the occurrence of any of the following events:
280	
281	> \(i\) any \"person\" or \"group\" (as such terms are used in Sections 13(d) and 14(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended) acquires \"beneficial ownership\" (as defined in Rule 13d-3 under the Exchange Act), directly or indirectly, of securities of the Company representing fifty percent (50%) or more of the combined voting power of the Company\'s then-outstanding voting securities entitled to vote generally in the election of directors;
282	>
283	> \(ii\) the individuals who, as of the Effective Date, constitute the Board (the \"**Incumbent Board**\") cease for any reason to constitute at least a majority of the Board; provided, however, that any individual who becomes a director of the Company subsequent to the Effective Date and whose election or nomination for election by the Company\'s stockholders was approved by a vote of at least a majority of the directors then comprising the Incumbent Board shall be considered as though such individual were a member of the Incumbent Board, but excluding, for this purpose, any such individual whose initial assumption of office occurs as a result of an actual or threatened election contest with respect to the election or removal of directors or other actual or threatened solicitation of proxies or consents by or on behalf of a person other than the Board;
284	>
285	> \(iii\) consummation of a merger, consolidation, statutory share exchange, or similar corporate transaction involving the Company or any of its subsidiaries (a \"**Business Combination**\"), unless, immediately following such Business Combination, (A) all or substantially all of the individuals and entities that were the beneficial owners of the Company\'s outstanding voting securities immediately prior to such Business Combination beneficially own, directly or indirectly, more than fifty percent (50%) of the combined voting power of the then-outstanding voting securities entitled to vote generally in the election of directors of the entity resulting from such Business Combination (including, without limitation, an entity that, as a result of such transaction, owns the Company or all or substantially all of the Company\'s assets either directly or through one or more subsidiaries), and (B) at least a majority of the members of the board of directors of the entity resulting from such Business Combination were members of the Incumbent Board at the time of the execution of the initial agreement or action of the Board providing for such Business Combination; or
286	>
287	> \(iv\) the sale or other disposition of all or substantially all of the assets of the Company to any person or entity that is not an Affiliate of the Company.
288	
289	**Section 11(b) --- Equity Acceleration upon Change in Control.** Upon the occurrence of a Change in Control, all outstanding unvested equity awards held by the Executive (including LTI Awards, the Make-Whole Award, and any other equity-based compensation granted to the Executive under any Company equity incentive plan or otherwise) shall immediately vest in full and become exercisable or nonforfeitable, without regard to whether the Executive\'s employment is terminated in connection with or following such Change in Control. In the case of PSUs, such awards shall vest at the target level of performance (i.e., 100% of the target number of PSUs). Settlement of vested awards shall occur within thirty (30) days following the Change in Control, subject to applicable tax withholdings.
290	
291	**Section 11(c) --- CIC Severance.** In the event the Executive\'s employment is terminated (I) by the Company without Cause, or (II) by the Executive for Good Reason, in either case within the twenty-four (24)-month period following a Change in Control (a \"**CIC Qualifying Termination**\"), then in lieu of (and not in addition to) the Severance Benefits set forth in Section 10.1, the Executive shall be entitled to the following:
292	
293	> \(i\) **CIC Cash Severance.** A lump-sum cash payment equal to three (3) times the sum of the Executive\'s then-current Base Salary plus the Executive\'s then-current Target Bonus, payable within thirty (30) calendar days following the date of termination, less all applicable withholdings and deductions. Based on the initial terms of this Agreement, such CIC cash severance amount is Four Million One Hundred Sixty-Two Thousand Five Hundred Dollars (\$4,162,500) (calculated as follows: \[\$750,000 + \$637,500\] × 3 = \$4,162,500).
294	>
295	> \(ii\) **Extended COBRA Continuation.** The Company shall pay or reimburse the cost of continued COBRA coverage (medical, dental, and vision) for the Executive and the Executive\'s eligible dependents for a period of thirty-six (36) months following the date of termination, on the same terms as set forth in Section 10.1(ii).
296	>
297	> \(iii\) **Pro-Rata Annual Bonus.** A pro-rata Annual Bonus for the fiscal year in which the termination occurs, with such pro-rata bonus to be no less than the Target Bonus, pro-rated for the number of days of service during such fiscal year, payable within thirty (30) calendar days following the date of termination.
298	>
299	> \(iv\) **Additional Equity Acceleration.** All outstanding equity awards not previously accelerated under Section 11(b) (including any awards granted between the Change in Control and the CIC Qualifying Termination) shall immediately vest and become exercisable or nonforfeitable as of the date of the CIC Qualifying Termination, with PSUs vesting at the greater of target performance or actual performance through the date of such termination.
300	
301	**Section 11(d) --- Section 280G Gross-Up.** In the event that any payment or benefit received or to be received by the Executive in connection with a Change in Control or the termination of the Executive\'s employment (whether pursuant to the terms of this Agreement, any equity incentive plan, any other plan, arrangement, or agreement with the Company, or otherwise) (such payments and benefits, together, the \"**Total Payments**\") would be subject to the excise tax imposed under Section 4999 of the Code (the \"**Excise Tax**\"), the Company shall pay the Executive an additional amount (the \"**Gross-Up Payment**\") such that, after payment of all taxes (including any income taxes, employment taxes, and any Excise Tax) imposed on the Gross-Up Payment and any interest or penalties with respect thereto, the Executive retains an amount of the Gross-Up Payment equal to the Excise Tax imposed on the Total Payments. The Gross-Up Payment is intended to place the Executive in the same after-tax position that the Executive would have been in had no Excise Tax been imposed on the Total Payments. The determination of whether any payment or benefit constitutes a \"parachute payment\" within the meaning of Section 280G of the Code, and the calculation of the Gross-Up Payment, shall be made by a nationally recognized accounting firm selected by the Company and reasonably acceptable to the Executive, and the costs of such determination shall be borne entirely by the Company.
302	
303	**[SECTION 12 --- RESTRICTIVE COVENANTS]{.underline}**
304	
305	**Section 12(a) --- Non-Competition.** During the Executive\'s employment with the Company and for a period of six (6) months following the termination of the Executive\'s employment for any reason (the \"**Restricted Period**\"), the Executive shall not, directly or indirectly, whether as an employee, consultant, advisor, officer, director, partner, member, stockholder, investor, agent, or in any other capacity:
306	
307	> \(i\) engage in, be employed by, consult for, or render services to any business, person, or entity that develops, manufactures, markets, distributes, or sells Directly Competitive Products;
308	>
309	> \(ii\) own, manage, operate, control, or participate in the ownership, management, operation, or control of any business, person, or entity that develops, manufactures, markets, distributes, or sells Directly Competitive Products; or
310	>
311	> \(iii\) assist any person or entity in doing any of the foregoing;
312	
313	provided, however, that nothing in this Section 12(a) shall prohibit the Executive from owning, directly or indirectly, less than two percent (2%) of the outstanding shares of any class of securities of any company that is listed on a national securities exchange or traded in the over-the-counter market.
314	
315	For purposes of this Agreement, \"**Directly Competitive Products**\" shall mean household cleaning products sold at retail in the United States, including without limitation surface cleaners, laundry detergents, dish soaps, disinfectants, and related household cleaning products that are competitive with the products manufactured, marketed, or distributed by the Company\'s Household Cleaning segment as of the date of the Executive\'s termination.
316	
317	**Section 12(b) --- Non-Solicitation of Employees.** During the Restricted Period, the Executive shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit, recruit, hire, or attempt to solicit, recruit, or hire any individual who was a direct report to the Executive at any time during the twelve (12)-month period preceding the termination of the Executive\'s employment, or encourage, induce, or attempt to encourage or induce any such individual to leave the employ of the Company or any of its Affiliates. For the avoidance of doubt, the restrictions of this Section 12(b) shall not apply to general solicitations of employment not specifically targeted at employees of the Company (such as advertisements in newspapers, trade publications, or on the internet), provided that the Executive does not direct such general solicitations toward specific employees of the Company.
318	
319	**Section 12(d) --- Garden Leave Compensation.** During the Restricted Period, the Company shall continue to pay the Executive her full Base Salary (at the rate in effect immediately prior to the termination of the Executive\'s employment) as \"garden leave\" compensation, payable in accordance with the Company\'s standard payroll practices, less all applicable tax withholdings and authorized deductions. Such garden leave payments shall be in addition to, and shall not offset or reduce, any severance, equity, bonus, or other payments to which the Executive may be entitled under this Agreement or any other plan, arrangement, or agreement with the Company. The Company\'s obligation to make garden leave payments under this Section 12(d) shall be unconditional and shall not be subject to the Executive\'s compliance with the restrictive covenants set forth in this Section 12 (i.e., the Company must make such payments regardless of whether the Executive breaches any covenant herein, although the Company\'s remedies for any such breach shall remain available).
320	
321	**Section 12(e) --- Reasonableness.** The Executive acknowledges and agrees that the restrictions set forth in this Section 12 are reasonable and necessary for the protection of the Company\'s legitimate business interests, including its Confidential Information, trade secrets, customer relationships, vendor relationships, and employee relationships. The Executive further acknowledges that the restrictions set forth herein are reasonable in scope, geographic area, and duration, and that the Executive has received adequate consideration for such restrictions in the form of the compensation and benefits provided under this Agreement. In the event a court of competent jurisdiction determines that any restriction set forth in this Section 12 is unreasonable or unenforceable in any respect, the Parties agree that the court shall have the authority to reform such restriction to the minimum extent necessary to make it enforceable, and such restriction, as so reformed, shall be binding upon the Parties.
322	
323	**Section 12(f) --- Equitable Relief.** The Executive acknowledges that a breach or threatened breach of the covenants set forth in this Section 12 would cause irreparable harm to the Company for which monetary damages would be an inadequate remedy, and the Company shall be entitled to seek temporary, preliminary, and permanent injunctive relief and specific performance, without the necessity of posting a bond or proving actual damages, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity. The Executive agrees that, in the event of any breach or threatened breach of this Section 12, the Restricted Period shall be tolled during the period of such breach.
324	
325	**[SECTION 13 --- INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY AND CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**
326	
327	**Section 13(a) --- Confidential Information.**
328	
329	**Definition.** For purposes of this Agreement, \"**Confidential Information**\" means all non-public information, whether written, oral, electronic, visual, or otherwise, relating to the business, operations, financial condition, technology, products, customers, suppliers, employees, strategies, or plans of the Company or any of its Affiliates, including without limitation: trade secrets; proprietary formulations and compositions; manufacturing processes and techniques; product development plans, roadmaps, and pipelines; research and development data; engineering designs and specifications; pricing strategies, models, and analyses; customer lists, customer data, and customer purchasing histories; vendor and supplier agreements, pricing, and terms; financial projections, budgets, and internal financial reports; marketing plans, strategies, and campaign data; strategic plans, acquisition targets, and business development initiatives; personnel information, compensation data, and organizational charts; information technology systems, software, and architecture; quality assurance protocols and testing methodologies; regulatory filings and compliance data; and any other information that the Company designates as confidential or that the Executive knows or reasonably should know is confidential based on the nature of the information or the circumstances of its disclosure.
330	
331	**Non-Disclosure.** During the Executive\'s employment and at all times thereafter, the Executive shall not, directly or indirectly, disclose, publish, communicate, furnish, or use for the benefit of any person or entity other than the Company or its Affiliates, any Confidential Information, except: (i) as required in the faithful performance of the Executive\'s duties hereunder; (ii) as required by applicable law, regulation, court order, or legal process (provided that, to the extent permitted by law, the Executive shall provide the Company with prompt written notice of such requirement so that the Company may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy); or (iii) with the prior written consent of the Company.
332	
333	**Carve-Out.** Notwithstanding the foregoing, \"Confidential Information\" shall not include information that: (i) is or becomes publicly available through no fault, act, or omission of the Executive; (ii) was lawfully known to the Executive prior to its disclosure by the Company, as evidenced by the Executive\'s contemporaneous written records; (iii) is lawfully received by the Executive from a third party who is not, to the Executive\'s knowledge, subject to any obligation of confidentiality with respect to such information; or (iv) constitutes the Executive\'s general knowledge, skills, and experience, including knowledge, skills, and experience acquired during the course of the Executive\'s employment with the Company.
334	
335	**Section 13(b) --- Return of Materials.** Upon termination of employment for any reason (or at any time upon the Company\'s request), the Executive shall promptly return to the Company all documents, files, records, correspondence, memoranda, notes, notebooks, reports, manuals, compilations, computer disks, flash drives, laptops, mobile devices, tablets, equipment, keys, access cards, and all other tangible and electronic property of the Company or its Affiliates in the Executive\'s possession, custody, or control, including all copies, summaries, excerpts, and derivatives thereof. The Executive shall permanently delete all electronic copies of Confidential Information from any personal devices, accounts, cloud storage services, or other media in the Executive\'s possession or control, and shall certify such deletion in writing to the Company upon request.
336	
337	**Section 13(c) --- Defend Trade Secrets Act Notice.** Pursuant to 18 U.S.C. § 1833(b), the Executive is hereby notified that the Executive shall not be held criminally or civilly liable under any federal or state trade secret law for the disclosure of a trade secret that is made: (i) in confidence to a federal, state, or local government official, either directly or indirectly, or to an attorney, solely for the purpose of reporting or investigating a suspected violation of law; or (ii) in a complaint or other document filed in a lawsuit or other proceeding, if such filing is made under seal. Additionally, an individual who files a lawsuit for retaliation by an employer for reporting a suspected violation of law may disclose a trade secret to the individual\'s attorney and use the trade secret information in the court proceeding, if the individual files any document containing the trade secret under seal and does not disclose the trade secret except pursuant to court order.
338	
339	**[SECTION 14 --- SECTION 280G]{.underline}**
340	
341	**Section 14.1 --- Excise Tax Gross-Up.** This Section 14 supplements and does not limit the Company\'s obligations under Section 11(d). In the event that any payment or benefit received or to be received by the Executive (whether under this Agreement, any equity incentive plan, any benefit plan, or otherwise) constitutes a \"parachute payment\" within the meaning of Section 280G of the Code and would be subject to the excise tax imposed by Section 4999 of the Code (the \"**Excise Tax**\"), the Company shall make an additional payment to the Executive (the \"**Gross-Up Payment**\") in an amount sufficient to place the Executive in the same after-tax position that the Executive would have been in had no Excise Tax been imposed on such payments or benefits. The Gross-Up Payment shall be calculated to cover the Excise Tax, any federal, state, and local income and employment taxes on the Gross-Up Payment itself, and any Excise Tax, interest, or penalties imposed on the Gross-Up Payment. The determination of whether any payment or benefit constitutes a \"parachute payment\" and the calculation of the Gross-Up Payment shall be made by a nationally recognized independent accounting firm selected by the Company and reasonably acceptable to the Executive (the \"**Accounting Firm**\"), and the costs and fees of the Accounting Firm shall be borne entirely by the Company. The Company and the Executive shall furnish to the Accounting Firm such information and documents as the Accounting Firm may reasonably request in order to make such determination and calculation. The Accounting Firm\'s determination shall be binding upon the Company and the Executive, absent manifest error.
342	
343	**Section 14.2 --- Timing of Gross-Up Payment.** Any Gross-Up Payment shall be made to the Executive no later than the end of the Executive\'s taxable year following the taxable year in which the Excise Tax is remitted to the applicable taxing authority (or, if no Excise Tax is remitted, the end of the Executive\'s taxable year following the taxable year in which an audit relating to such Excise Tax is completed or there is a final and non-appealable settlement or other resolution of such matter). In the event that the Excise Tax is later determined by the Internal Revenue Service or a court of competent jurisdiction to be greater than the amount taken into account in calculating the initial Gross-Up Payment, the Company shall make an additional Gross-Up Payment to the Executive within thirty (30) days of such determination. In the event that the Excise Tax is later determined to be less than the amount taken into account in calculating the initial Gross-Up Payment, the Executive shall refund the excess portion of the Gross-Up Payment to the Company within thirty (30) days of such determination, provided that the Executive shall have no obligation to make any such refund to the extent it would place the Executive in an after-tax position that is less favorable than the position the Executive would have been in had the Excise Tax and the Gross-Up Payment been properly calculated initially.

Each Party hereby irrevocably consents to the personal jurisdiction and venue of such courts and waives any objection to such jurisdiction or venue, including any objection based on inconvenient forum. Each Party agrees that service of process in any such action may be effected by delivering the relevant documents in the manner specified in Section 16.7 (Notices).

The Company shall advance all reasonable attorneys\' fees and expenses incurred by the Executive in connection with any such claim promptly upon the Executive\'s request therefor, subject to the Executive\'s delivery of an undertaking to repay such advances if it is ultimately determined by a court of competent jurisdiction in a final, non-appealable judgment that the Executive is not entitled to indemnification. The rights of the Executive under this Section 16.1 shall be in addition to, and not in lieu of, any other rights the Executive may have under the Company\'s Certificate of Incorporation, Bylaws, any separate indemnification agreement, or applicable law. Any purported assignment by the Executive in violation of this Section 16.8 shall be void and of no force or effect. The Company may assign this Agreement to any successor to all or substantially all of the business and/or assets of the Company (whether by merger, consolidation, reorganization, sale of assets, or otherwise), and the Company shall require any such successor to expressly assume and agree to perform this Agreement in the same manner and to the same extent that the Company would be required to perform it if no such succession had taken place. """Validate a .docx for delivery.

Checks ZIP integrity, XML well-formedness for every part, [Content_Types].xml
presence, and relationship consistency (no dangling rIds). Does NOT do XSD
schema validation in v1 — defer until ECMA-376 XSDs are vendored fresh from
ECMA-International.

Usage: python validate.py file.docx
Exit 0 = valid; non-zero = errors printed to stderr.
"""
import sys
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path
from lxml import etree


def validate(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    errors = []

    if not path.exists():
        return [f"File not found: {path}"]
    if not zipfile.is_zipfile(path):
        return [f"Not a valid ZIP: {path}"]

    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:
        names = set(z.namelist())

        if "[Content_Types].xml" not in names:
            errors.append("Missing [Content_Types].xml")
            return errors

        # XML well-formedness for every .xml and .rels part
        for name in names:
            if name.endswith(".xml") or name.endswith(".rels"):
                try:
                    etree.fromstring(z.read(name))
                except etree.XMLSyntaxError as e:
                    errors.append(f"Malformed XML in {name}: {e}")

        # Relationship target consistency
        for rels_name in [n for n in names if n.endswith(".rels")]:
            try:
                rels = etree.fromstring(z.read(rels_name))
            except etree.XMLSyntaxError:
                continue
            ns = "{http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/package/2006/relationships}"
            for rel in rels.findall(f"{ns}Relationship"):
                target = rel.get("Target") or ""
                target_mode = rel.get("TargetMode", "Internal")
                if target_mode == "External" or target.startswith(("http", "mailto:")):
                    continue
                # Targets starting with "/" are package-absolute (root-relative).
                # Others are relative to the .rels file's parent directory.
                if target.startswith("/"):
                    target_norm = target.lstrip("/")
                else:
                    rels_path = Path(rels_name)
                    base_dir = rels_path.parent.parent if rels_path.parent.name == "_rels" else rels_path.parent
                    target_norm = (base_dir / target).as_posix()
                parts = []
                for seg in target_norm.split("/"):
                    if seg == ".." and parts:
                        parts.pop()
                    elif seg and seg != ".":
                        parts.append(seg)
                target_norm = "/".join(parts)
                if target_norm not in names:
                    errors.append(f"Dangling relationship in {rels_name}: target {target!r} not found")

    return errors


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 2:
        print("Usage: validate.py <file>", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(2)
    errs = validate(Path(sys.argv[1]))
    if errs:
        for e in errs:
            print(f"ERROR: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
