  draft='Defines \"CPI\" (salary escalator), \"Peer Group Companies\" (LTI floor) and \"Directly Competitive Products\" (narrow non-compete). Several capitalized terms used in the draft are never defined: \"Accrued Obligations\" is defined only in Section 10.3, and \"Exchange Act\" is never defined.',
  base='The playbook (Sections II, V and VIII) prohibits salary escalators and peer-group LTI floors and requires a non-compete covering all business lines.',
  analysis=['These definitions exist only to support provisions we are deleting. If they stay in, they invite arguments that the concepts survive elsewhere in the agreement. Add definitions for the new defined terms in the counter-draft: Plan, Clawback Policy, Release, Section 409A, Competing Business, Restricted Territory, Non-Compete Period, CIC Protection Period, Qualifying Termination and Exchange Act.'],
  redline=['[-\"CPI\" means the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), U.S. City Average, All Items, as published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. In the event the CPI is discontinued or substantially revised, the Parties shall substitute a comparable index published by a governmental agency.-]',
           '[-\"Directly Competitive Products\" has the meaning set forth in Section 12(a).-]{+\"Competing Business\" and \"Restricted Territory\" have the meanings set forth in Section 12(a).+}',
           '[-\"Peer Group Companies\" has the meaning set forth in Section 6(a).-]{+\"Plan\" means the Pinnacle Consumer Brands, Inc. 2022 Omnibus [Equity] Incentive Plan, as amended from time to time, or any successor plan.+}',
           '{+\"Clawback Policy\" has the meaning set forth in Section 18. \"Release\" has the meaning set forth in Section 10.2. \"Section 409A\" has the meaning set forth in Section 17. \"Exchange Act\" means the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended.+}'],
  comment='Conforming changes to the definitions to reflect the revisions in Sections 3, 6, 12 and the new Sections 17 and 18.',
  params='Bracketed plan name: the term sheet calls it the \"2022 Omnibus Equity Incentive Plan\", while the playbook and the draft call it the \"2022 Omnibus Incentive Plan\". Confirm the exact title against the plan document or proxy before circulating.'),
 ])

sec('Section 1 - Position and Duties',
 'Section 1 contains three governance provisions that the term sheet and playbook flatly prohibit: the Board nomination covenant, the minimum direct-reports covenant and the office specification. Two of them are also wired into Good Reason. Section 1.6, on Meridian, is the main non-economic risk item in the draft.',
 [
 dict(id='3', sec='1.1', title='Enumerated functional portfolio can be used to build Good Reason claims',
  sev='Low', cat=NG, impact='Indirect. Feeds the \"material diminution\" Good Reason trigger',
  draft='Lists specific functions (operations, manufacturing, supply chain, quality assurance, procurement, distribution) under the COO and uses \"consistent with and customary for.\"',
  base='Playbook Section X standard language: duties \"as are customary for such position ... and as may be assigned from time to time by the [CEO], consistent with the Executive\'s position.\"',
  analysis=['Listing functions is not prohibited, but each function listed becomes a benchmark for a \"material diminution\" claim if the Company later reorganizes. A likely example is moving procurement into a shared-services function during the Harmony Pet Naturals integration. We recommend keeping the list as descriptive only and adding a reallocation right.'],
  redline=['... distribution, and such other duties, responsibilities, and authority as are [-consistent with and -]customary for the position of Chief Operating Officer of a publicly traded consumer products company of similar size and complexity{+ and as may be assigned from time to time by the CEO, consistent with the Executive\'s position. The Company may reallocate particular functions among its executive officers from time to time, and no such reallocation shall by itself constitute Good Reason unless it results in a material diminution in the Executive\'s authority, duties, or responsibilities taken as a whole+}.'],
  comment='Conformed to the Company\'s standard formulation for executive-officer duties. Added an express right to reallocate functions so that ordinary reorganizations do not trigger Good Reason.',
  params='Can concede the descriptive list of functions. Hold the \"as may be assigned by the CEO\" language and the reallocation sentence.'),
 dict(id='4', sec='1.2', title='Board nomination commitment',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Non-economic, but it creates a Good Reason trigger (Section 9(b)(v)) that would unlock $2.775M of draft severance ($1.575M under the term sheet)',
  draft='\"The Company shall nominate the Executive to serve on the Board ... within twelve (12) months\" and use \"reasonable best efforts\" to place her on the management slate.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 2: Board nomination \"is not part of the approved compensation package\" and the agreement \"shall not include any commitment, promise, or expectation\" regarding nomination. Playbook Sections VI.D and X prohibit board-seat commitments, \"whether binding or precatory.\"',
  analysis=['Pinnacle is a Delaware corporation. Under DGCL Section 141(a), the business and affairs of the corporation, including the slate of nominees, are managed by the Board. Director nominations run through the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee under its charter and NYSE Section 303A.04. A contractual commitment by the Company to nominate an officer either fetters the directors\' future exercise of fiduciary judgment, which makes it vulnerable as unenforceable, or creates an implied contract right that the Executive could enforce through damages or Good Reason. Either outcome is unacceptable.',
           'An insider director would also affect Board composition: the CEO already sits on the Board, and NYSE Section 303A.01 requires a majority of independent directors. The item is also directly linked to severance through Section 9(b)(v).'],
  redline=['Section 1.2 - [-Board Nomination. The Company shall nominate the Executive to serve on the Board of Directors of the Company within twelve (12) months of the Effective Date. ... During any period in which the Executive serves as a member of the Board, the Executive shall be subject to all applicable fiduciary duties and governance policies applicable to directors of the Company.-]{+No Board Commitment. The Executive acknowledges that nomination and election of directors are within the sole discretion of the Board, its Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee and the Company\'s stockholders, and that nothing in this Agreement constitutes a commitment, promise, or expectation regarding the Executive\'s nomination, appointment or election to the Board. If the Executive is ever elected or appointed to the Board or the board of any Affiliate, she shall serve without additional compensation and shall resign from such position(s) upon the termination of her employment for any reason.+}'],
  comment='Director nominations are reserved to the Board and its Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee in the exercise of their fiduciary duties, and the Company cannot contract to bind that judgment. Replaced with a customary acknowledgment and a resignation-on-termination undertaking.'),
 dict(id='5', sec='1.3', title='Minimum of eight direct reports; reduction = Good Reason',
  sev='High', cat=MR, impact='Non-economic, but a reorganization could trigger full severance (draft $2.775M; CIC $4.16M)',
  draft='Executive shall have \"no fewer than eight (8) direct reports,\" including named heads for each of four segments. Any reduction below eight is Good Reason.',
  base='Playbook Section X prohibits any minimum number of direct reports or required reporting functions. Playbook Section VI.D prohibits a direct-reports Good Reason trigger.',
  analysis=['This is a hair trigger. Ordinary integration activity, such as consolidating Harmony Pet Naturals operations into an existing segment or merging the supply chain and procurement leadership roles, would let the Executive resign and collect full severance. It also hands the Executive a veto over the CEO\'s organizational design.'],
  redline=['Section 1.3 - [-Direct Reports. The Executive shall have no fewer than eight (8) direct reports, including the heads of manufacturing, supply chain, quality assurance, and operations for each of the Company\'s business segments (currently Household Cleaning, Personal Care, Specialty Food, and Pet Care). Any reduction in the number of the Executive\'s direct reports below eight (8) without the Executive\'s prior written consent shall constitute Good Reason as defined in Section 9(b). The Company shall provide the Executive with an updated organizational chart within thirty (30) days of the Effective Date reflecting the Executive\'s direct reporting relationships.-]{+[Reserved].+}'],
  comment='Organizational structure and reporting lines remain within management\'s discretion. The Executive\'s protection against a genuine demotion is the \"material diminution\" Good Reason trigger in Section 9(b)(i).'),
 dict(id='6', sec='1.4', title='Office specification (400 sq. ft., executive floor)',
  sev='Low', cat=NG, impact='Nominal cost. Creates a breach-of-contract hook usable as a Good Reason trigger under Section 9(b)(vi)',
  draft='Private office of not less than 400 square feet on the executive floor, ready by the Effective Date.',
  base='Playbook Section X: no office size, floor location or amenity specifications. Playbook Section VI.D prohibits office specifications as Good Reason triggers.',
  analysis=['The cost is trivial. The issue is that any failure to provide the office becomes a \"material breach\" under Good Reason clause (vi). Replace with a general commitment.'],
  redline=['Section 1.4 - Office. The Executive shall be provided with [-a private office of not less than four hundred (400) square feet on the executive floor of-]{+office space and administrative support at+} the Company\'s principal offices at 4200 Tryon Ridge Parkway, Suite 1100, Charlotte, NC 28217[-. Such office shall be furnished and equipped in a manner-]{+, in each case+} consistent with [-the offices-]{+those+} provided to other members of the Company\'s senior executive team[-. The Company shall ensure that the Executive\'s office is available and ready for occupancy no later than the Effective Date-].'],
  comment='Replaced the physical specifications with a parity standard consistent with the Company\'s executive office policy.',
  params='Can offer an informal side assurance from Kendra Millstone about office location. Do not include specifications in the contract.'),
 dict(id='7', sec='1.5(a)', title='Outside for-profit boards (up to two)',
  sev='Low', cat=NG, impact='Non-economic. Time-commitment, conflict and insider-trading considerations',
  draft='Executive may serve on up to two for-profit boards with advance Board approval.',
  base='Neither the term sheet nor the playbook addresses this.',
  analysis=['Board approval is already required, which mitigates the risk. For a newly hired COO in the middle of an integration, one outside public or private company board is market.   redline=['(a) serve on the board of directors or advisory board of up to [-two (2)-]{+one (1)+} for-profit [-entities-]{+entity+} (excluding the Company), provided that such service is approved in advance by the [-Board-]{+CEO and the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee in accordance with the Company\'s policies on outside directorships+}{+, such entity is not engaged in a Competing Business,+} and [-does-]{+such service does+} not create a conflict of interest with, or interfere with the performance of, the Executive\'s duties hereunder;'],
  comment='Conformed outside-board service to the Company\'s outside directorship policy and excluded competitors.',

 ])
EOF"

input.command:
S=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/sbx.sh; R=/home/user/Lawless_Research_Lab/harvey_lab/vendor/harvey-labs/results/employment-labor/draft-markup-of-executive-employment-agreement/claude-code-session/20261015-113620; $S $R "cat > /workspace/build/content2.py <<'EOF'
# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
from content1 import SECTIONS, sec, MR, NG

SECTIONS[-1]['issues'].append(
 dict(id='8', sec='1.6', title='PRIORITY FLAG - Meridian non-compete overlap: inadequate representation; Company bears the compliance burden',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Third-party tortious-interference and injunction exposure (not quantifiable until we have the Meridian agreement). Possible delay or disruption of start',
  draft='Executive represents her employment \"will not breach\" prior obligations, but in the same sentence \"represents that her duties hereunder shall be structured\" through March 15, 2026 to avoid violating the Meridian Non-Compete. The parties \"work together in good faith\" to define her duties. She discloses the Meridian terms only \"upon request.\"',
  base='Partner instruction: (a) flag prominently, (b) obtain and review the Meridian non-compete before the agreement is finalized, and (c) add an Executive representation and warranty of non-violation. Term Sheet Section 1 notes the 12-month Meridian non-compete expiring March 15, 2026.',
  analysis=['Overlap. The proposed start date of January 6, 2026 falls 68 days (about 10 weeks) before the Meridian covenant expires on March 15, 2026. During that window she would be COO of a direct competitor in household cleaning and personal care. Meridian is a \"Home & Health\" company, so its product lines likely overlap with Pinnacle\'s.',
           'Why the draft is dangerous for Pinnacle. The draft documents Pinnacle\'s actual knowledge of the covenant in both the recital and Section 1.6. Knowledge of the contract is the element plaintiffs usually find hardest to prove in a tortious-interference claim. The draft then makes duty-structuring a joint obligation, which arguably puts the compliance burden on the Company. Worse, any duty restriction the Company imposes to keep her clear of Meridian could itself be pleaded as a \"material diminution\" Good Reason trigger under draft Section 9(b)(i) or the catch-all in 9(b)(vii). Under the draft, that would entitle her to $2.775M in cash severance with no release.',
           'Facts we must resolve. (1) The timeline does not reconcile. A 12-month post-employment covenant expiring March 15, 2026 implies a separation date of about March 15, 2025, yet both the term sheet and the draft say she \"currently serves\" at Meridian. Either the covenant runs from a fixed date other than separation (for example, a role change or an agreement date), or she is already in a notice or garden-leave status, or the expiry date is wrong. If the covenant actually runs 12 months from her future separation, the overlap could be about a full year rather than about 10 weeks. (2) The term sheet states that RPV \"has reviewed the Meridian agreement,\" but your October 4 email asks us to obtain a copy. We have no copy in the file and should confirm whether one exists. (3) Minnesota law: Minn. Stat. Section 181.988 voids most employee non-competes entered into on or after July 1, 2023. If the Meridian covenant pre-dates that law, it is enforceable under Minnesota\'s reasonableness standard. If it was signed or refreshed later (for example, with an equity grant), it may be void. The agreement date, governing law and forum clause of the Meridian covenant therefore matter. (4) We need the scope of the Meridian non-solicit and confidentiality covenants, which are typically longer than 12 months, because they will constrain her hiring of Meridian talent.',
           'Recommended protections (reflected in the redline): (i) full Executive representations and warranties, including no Meridian confidential information; (ii) delivery of all prior covenant agreements before signing, as a condition to the Company\'s obligations; (iii) a Company right to restrict or reassign duties during the Transition Period without triggering Good Reason; (iv) a Company right to defer the Effective Date to March 16, 2026; (v) a prompt-notice covenant; and (vi) Cause for any material misrepresentation. Business options for TJ: (A) defer the start to March 16, 2026, which is the cleanest option and moves the 2026 bonus proration and the vesting dates; (B) start on January 6 with a documented transition-duties plan limited to non-competitive work (for example, integration planning that does not touch competing product lines) and no access to competitively sensitive information; or (C) seek a written waiver or consent from Meridian. Under option A or B, the Company should not agree to indemnify or defend the Executive against Meridian claims in the employment agreement. Any decision on defense costs should be made later and case by case.'],
  redline=['Section 1.6 - [-Compliance with Existing Obligations. The Executive represents and warrants that her employment with the Company and the performance of her duties hereunder will not breach any obligation to any prior employer, ... The Executive shall promptly disclose to the Company the full terms and conditions of the Meridian Non-Compete, and shall provide the Company with a copy thereof upon request.-]{+Prior Obligations; Representations and Warranties.+}',
           '{+(a) The Executive represents and warrants to the Company that: (i) prior to the date of this Agreement she has delivered to the Company true and complete copies of every agreement, plan, award agreement and policy acknowledgment containing any non-competition, non-solicitation, no-hire, confidentiality, invention assignment or other restrictive covenant by which she is bound, including all such agreements with Meridian Home & Health Corp. (\"Meridian\") (collectively, the \"Prior Covenants\"); (ii) other than the non-competition covenant in favor of Meridian that expires on March 15, 2026 (the \"Meridian Non-Compete\"), no Prior Covenant prohibits or materially restricts her employment with the Company or the performance of her duties hereunder; (iii) her execution of this Agreement, commencement of employment on the Effective Date and performance of her duties hereunder will not breach any Prior Covenant or any other agreement, order or obligation by which she is bound; and (iv) she has not taken or retained, and will not use or disclose in the course of her employment with the Company, any confidential or proprietary information or trade secrets of Meridian or any other former employer.+}',
           '{+(b) From the Effective Date through March 15, 2026 (the \"Transition Period\"), the Executive shall not perform any services that would breach the Meridian Non-Compete. The Company may, in its sole discretion and after consultation with the Executive, limit, defer or reassign any of the Executive\'s duties, responsibilities, reporting relationships, access to information or business-unit oversight to the extent the Company determines advisable to avoid any actual or alleged breach of the Prior Covenants, whether during the Transition Period or in response to any actual or threatened claim by Meridian. No such action shall constitute Good Reason or a breach of this Agreement.+}',
           '{+(c) The Company\'s obligations under this Agreement are conditioned upon the Company\'s receipt and review, with results satisfactory to the Company in its reasonable discretion, of the Prior Covenants. If the Company reasonably determines prior to the Effective Date that the Executive\'s commencement of employment on January 6, 2026 presents a material risk of breach of the Meridian Non-Compete, the Company may, by written notice to the Executive, defer the Effective Date to a date not later than March 16, 2026, in which case all dates in this Agreement measured from the Effective Date shall be adjusted accordingly.+}',
           '{+(d) The Executive shall notify the Company promptly in writing of any communication from Meridian or any other former employer concerning any Prior Covenant. Any material inaccuracy in the representations and warranties in Section 1.6(a) shall constitute Cause under Section 9(a)(ix).+}'],
  comment='Before the agreement is executed, we need copies of all prior restrictive covenant agreements, including the Meridian agreement. The revised Section 1.6 gives full representations of non-conflict and of non-use of prior-employer confidential information. It also gives the Company the flexibility to manage the Transition Period, including deferring the start date, without that flexibility being treated as Good Reason.',
  params='Negotiable within limits: (1) whether the Effective Date is deferred or a transition-duties plan is used (business call); (2) a cap on how far the Effective Date can be deferred (we propose March 16, 2026); (3) a mutual consultation obligation. Non-negotiable: delivery of the Meridian agreement before signing, the non-conflict representation, and no Good Reason from transition restrictions. Do not agree to a Company indemnity for Meridian claims in the agreement.'))

sec('Section 2 - Term',
 'The draft converts Company non-renewal into a full-severance event and doubles the non-renewal notice period. Together, these turn a three-year fixed term into a guaranteed severance entitlement at the end of each term.',
 [
 dict(id='9', sec='2.2', title='Non-renewal notice of 180 days (vs. 90 days)',
  sev='Medium', cat=MR, impact='Locks the Company in for 90 extra days per renewal cycle. Combined with Issue 10, roughly 0.5 years of compensation exposure per cycle',
  draft='Either party must give 180 days\' notice of non-renewal.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 3 and Playbook Section XI: 90 days. Longer periods are \"not standard\" and need Committee approval.',
  analysis=['Doubling the notice period lengthens the window in which the Company is committed and, under draft Section 2.3, makes the severance windfall harder to avoid.'],
  redline=['... unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal to the other Party at least [-one hundred eighty (180)-]{+ninety (90)+} days prior to the expiration of the then-current Term. ... For the avoidance of doubt, the obligation to provide [-one hundred eighty (180)-]{+ninety (90)+} days\' advance notice of non-renewal applies to both the Company and the Executive, ...'],
  comment='Conformed the non-renewal notice period to 90 days, which is the Company\'s standard for executive officers.'),
 dict(id='10', sec='2.3; 9(f); 10.1', title='Company non-renewal treated as a termination without Cause (full severance)',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='At year-3 draft rates: $3,059,437.50 cash + 24 months COBRA (~$60,000) + garden leave $413,437.50 = ~$3.53M, vs. $0 under the term sheet (accrued obligations only)',
  draft='Company non-renewal \"shall be treated for all purposes ... as a termination by the Company without Cause\" and triggers all Severance Benefits. Executive non-renewal is treated as a resignation. The same point is repeated in Section 9(f) and Section 10.1(a).',
  base='Term Sheet Section 3: non-renewal by the Company \"shall not constitute a termination without Cause and shall not trigger severance\". Accrued compensation only. Playbook Section XI: such provisions are \"not acceptable\".',
  analysis=['This provision guarantees a severance payment at the end of the term even if the Company offers renewal on similar terms. It sits on top of the elevated severance formula. At year-3 draft rates (base $826,875 after two 5% escalators; target bonus $702,843.75), Company non-renewal on January 5, 2029 would cost $3,059,437.50 in cash severance (24 months of base plus 2x target), plus 24 months of COBRA and 6 months of unconditional garden leave ($413,437.50). The term sheet obligation is $0.',
           'Note: the playbook would allow a 6-month transition payment (about $350,000) plus a pro-rata actual bonus on Company non-renewal, with Committee approval. The approved term sheet does not include one. Because TJ will not return to the Committee, that fallback is not available and should not be offered.'],
  redline=['Section 2.3 - Effect of Non-Renewal. [-In the event the Company provides notice of non-renewal pursuant to Section 2.2, such non-renewal shall be treated for all purposes of this Agreement as a termination by the Company without Cause, and the Executive shall be entitled to all Severance Benefits set forth in Section 10 as if her employment had been terminated by the Company without Cause on the last day of the then-current Term. For the avoidance of doubt, in the event the Executive provides notice of non-renewal pursuant to Section 2.2, such non-renewal shall be treated as a voluntary resignation by the Executive without Good Reason, and the Executive shall be entitled only to Accrued Obligations as set forth in Section 10.3.-]{+Non-renewal of the Term by either Party in accordance with Section 2.2 shall not constitute a termination by the Company without Cause or a resignation by the Executive for Good Reason, and shall not entitle the Executive to the Severance Benefits or the CIC Severance Benefits. Upon the expiration of the Term following a notice of non-renewal by either Party, the Executive\'s employment shall terminate and the Executive shall be entitled only to the Accrued Obligations, together with any Annual Bonus earned for a completed fiscal year but not yet paid as of the date of termination (payable at the time it would otherwise have been paid).+}',
           'Section 9(f) - [-Expiration/Non-Renewal. For the avoidance of doubt, in the event the Company provides notice of non-renewal of the Term pursuant to Section 2.2, such non-renewal shall be treated as a termination by the Company without Cause, ... The provisions of Section 2.3 are hereby incorporated by reference into this Section 9(f).-]{+Expiration/Non-Renewal. The consequences of non-renewal of the Term are set forth exclusively in Section 2.3.+}',
           'Section 10.1 - ... terminated (a) by the Company without Cause [-(including a non-renewal pursuant to Sections 2.3 and 9(f))-], or (b) by the Executive for Good Reason ...'],
  comment='Non-renewal is a separate event from a termination without Cause. The Company has offered a three-year term with automatic renewal, and a guaranteed severance payment at the end of the term is not something the Company can agree to.'),
 dict(id='11', sec='2.4', title='\"At will\" language conflicts with fixed term and severance architecture',
  sev='Low', cat=NG, impact='Drafting ambiguity. Litigation risk over whether the term is guaranteed',
  draft='Employment is \"at will\" \"notwithstanding\" the three-year term, but the Company \"acknowledges its obligations\" to pay compensation during employment and severance.',

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
from content1 import SECTIONS, sec, MR, NG

SECTIONS[-1]['issues'].append(
 dict(id='8', sec='1.6', title='PRIORITY FLAG - Meridian non-compete overlap: inadequate representation; Company bears the compliance burden',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Third-party tortious-interference and injunction exposure (not quantifiable until we have the Meridian agreement). Possible delay or disruption of start',
  draft='Executive represents her employment \"will not breach\" prior obligations, but in the same sentence \"represents that her duties hereunder shall be structured\" through March 15, 2026 to avoid violating the Meridian Non-Compete. The parties \"work together in good faith\" to define her duties. She discloses the Meridian terms only \"upon request.\"',
  base='Partner instruction: (a) flag prominently, (b) obtain and review the Meridian non-compete before the agreement is finalized, and (c) add an Executive representation and warranty of non-violation. Term Sheet Section 1 notes the 12-month Meridian non-compete expiring March 15, 2026.',
  analysis=['Overlap. The proposed start date of January 6, 2026 falls 68 days (about 10 weeks) before the Meridian covenant expires on March 15, 2026. During that window she would be COO of a direct competitor in household cleaning and personal care. Meridian is a \"Home & Health\" company, so its product lines likely overlap with Pinnacle\'s.',
           'Why the draft is dangerous for Pinnacle. The draft documents Pinnacle\'s actual knowledge of the covenant in both the recital and Section 1.6. Knowledge of the contract is the element plaintiffs usually find hardest to prove in a tortious-interference claim. The draft then makes duty-structuring a joint obligation, which arguably puts the compliance burden on the Company. Worse, any duty restriction the Company imposes to keep her clear of Meridian could itself be pleaded as a \"material diminution\" Good Reason trigger under draft Section 9(b)(i) or the catch-all in 9(b)(vii). Under the draft, that would entitle her to $2.775M in cash severance with no release.',
           'Facts we must resolve. (1) The timeline does not reconcile. A 12-month post-employment covenant expiring March 15, 2026 implies a separation date of about March 15, 2025, yet both the term sheet and the draft say she \"currently serves\" at Meridian. Either the covenant runs from a fixed date other than separation (for example, a role change or an agreement date), or she is already in a notice or garden-leave status, or the expiry date is wrong. If the covenant actually runs 12 months from her future separation, the overlap could be about a full year rather than about 10 weeks. (2) The term sheet states that RPV \"has reviewed the Meridian agreement,\" but your October 4 email asks us to obtain a copy. We have no copy in the file and should confirm whether one exists. (3) Minnesota law: Minn. Stat. Section 181.988 voids most employee non-competes entered into on or after July 1, 2023. If the Meridian covenant pre-dates that law, it is enforceable under Minnesota\'s reasonableness standard. If it was signed or refreshed later (for example, with an equity grant), it may be void. The agreement date, governing law and forum clause of the Meridian covenant therefore matter. (4) We need the scope of the Meridian non-solicit and confidentiality covenants, which are typically longer than 12 months, because they will constrain her hiring of Meridian talent.',
           'Recommended protections (reflected in the redline): (i) full Executive representations and warranties, including no Meridian confidential information; (ii) delivery of all prior covenant agreements before signing, as a condition to the Company\'s obligations; (iii) a Company right to restrict or reassign duties during the Transition Period without triggering Good Reason; (iv) a Company right to defer the Effective Date to March 16, 2026; (v) a prompt-notice covenant; and (vi) Cause for any material misrepresentation. Business options for TJ: (A) defer the start to March 16, 2026, which is the cleanest option and moves the 2026 bonus proration and the vesting dates; (B) start on January 6 with a documented transition-duties plan limited to non-competitive work (for example, integration planning that does not touch competing product lines) and no access to competitively sensitive information; or (C) seek a written waiver or consent from Meridian. Under option A or B, the Company should not agree to indemnify or defend the Executive against Meridian claims in the employment agreement. Any decision on defense costs should be made later and case by case.'],
  redline=['Section 1.6 - [-Compliance with Existing Obligations. The Executive represents and warrants that her employment with the Company and the performance of her duties hereunder will not breach any obligation to any prior employer, ... The Executive shall promptly disclose to the Company the full terms and conditions of the Meridian Non-Compete, and shall provide the Company with a copy thereof upon request.-]{+Prior Obligations; Representations and Warranties.+}',
           '{+(a) The Executive represents and warrants to the Company that: (i) prior to the date of this Agreement she has delivered to the Company true and complete copies of every agreement, plan, award agreement and policy acknowledgment containing any non-competition, non-solicitation, no-hire, confidentiality, invention assignment or other restrictive covenant by which she is bound, including all such agreements with Meridian Home & Health Corp. (\"Meridian\") (collectively, the \"Prior Covenants\"); (ii) other than the non-competition covenant in favor of Meridian that expires on March 15, 2026 (the \"Meridian Non-Compete\"), no Prior Covenant prohibits or materially restricts her employment with the Company or the performance of her duties hereunder; (iii) her execution of this Agreement, commencement of employment on the Effective Date and performance of her duties hereunder will not breach any Prior Covenant or any other agreement, order or obligation by which she is bound; and (iv) she has not taken or retained, and will not use or disclose in the course of her employment with the Company, any confidential or proprietary information or trade secrets of Meridian or any other former employer.+}',
           '{+(b) From the Effective Date through March 15, 2026 (the \"Transition Period\"), the Executive shall not perform any services that would breach the Meridian Non-Compete. The Company may, in its sole discretion and after consultation with the Executive, limit, defer or reassign any of the Executive\'s duties, responsibilities, reporting relationships, access to information or business-unit oversight to the extent the Company determines advisable to avoid any actual or alleged breach of the Prior Covenants, whether during the Transition Period or in response to any actual or threatened claim by Meridian. No such action shall constitute Good Reason or a breach of this Agreement.+}',
           '{+(c) The Company\'s obligations under this Agreement are conditioned upon the Company\'s receipt and review, with results satisfactory to the Company in its reasonable discretion, of the Prior Covenants. If the Company reasonably determines prior to the Effective Date that the Executive\'s commencement of employment on January 6, 2026 presents a material risk of breach of the Meridian Non-Compete, the Company may, by written notice to the Executive, defer the Effective Date to a date not later than March 16, 2026, in which case all dates in this Agreement measured from the Effective Date shall be adjusted accordingly.+}',
           '{+(d) The Executive shall notify the Company promptly in writing of any communication from Meridian or any other former employer concerning any Prior Covenant. Any material inaccuracy in the representations and warranties in Section 1.6(a) shall constitute Cause under Section 9(a)(ix).+}'],
  comment='Before the agreement is executed, we need copies of all prior restrictive covenant agreements, including the Meridian agreement. The revised Section 1.6 gives full representations of non-conflict and of non-use of prior-employer confidential information. It also gives the Company the flexibility to manage the Transition Period, including deferring the start date, without that flexibility being treated as Good Reason.',
  params='Negotiable within limits: (1) whether the Effective Date is deferred or a transition-duties plan is used (business call); (2) a cap on how far the Effective Date can be deferred (we propose March 16, 2026); (3) a mutual consultation obligation. Non-negotiable: delivery of the Meridian agreement before signing, the non-conflict representation, and no Good Reason from transition restrictions. Do not agree to a Company indemnity for Meridian claims in the agreement.'))

sec('Section 9 - Termination (Cause and Good Reason)',
 'The draft\'s Cause definition is almost impossible to satisfy, and its Good Reason definition can be triggered by routine management decisions. Taken together with the elevated severance and the absence of a release, the Company could almost never terminate her for Cause, and the Executive could almost always find a basis to resign for Good Reason and collect severance. This is the structural core of the draft and has to be rebuilt.',
 [
 dict(id='36', sec='9(a)', title='Cause limited to felony, embezzlement >\$10,000, and uncured material breach (60-day cure); 2/3 Board vote; good-faith defense',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Effectively converts misconduct terminations into without-Cause terminations: \$2.775M draft severance (\$1.575M term sheet) plus loss of signing bonus/relocation clawbacks',
  draft='Three grounds only: (i) felony conviction or plea; (ii) willful embezzlement exceeding \$10,000; (iii) material breach uncured within 60 days. Procedural overlay: specific notice, hearing before at least three independent directors, approval by two-thirds of the Board, and a blanket \"good faith\" defense.',
  base='Playbook Section VI.C requires all eight grounds: felony/moral turpitude; embezzlement/fraud; gross negligence or willful misconduct; material breach of fiduciary duty; material breach of agreement or covenants; material policy/Code violation; willful refusal to perform; and dishonesty causing harm. A 30-day cure applies only to grounds (v) to (vii). Playbook Section VI.C states that narrow definitions are \"prohibited.\"',
  analysis=['The draft omits gross negligence, willful misconduct, fiduciary breach, policy violations (harassment, insider trading, FCPA), willful refusal and dishonesty. The \$10,000 threshold would excuse smaller embezzlement. The good-faith defense borrows the DGCL Section 145 indemnification standard and would defeat Cause for almost any conduct she claims to have believed was in the Company\'s interest. The two-thirds supermajority lets a minority of directors block a Cause termination.',
           'Our redline includes one deliberate give: an opportunity to be heard before the Board, with counsel. It costs little and improves the defensibility of any Cause determination. A ninth ground covers material misrepresentation in the Meridian representations (Section 1.6).'],
  redline=['Section 9(a) - Cause. [-For purposes of this Agreement, \"Cause\" shall mean the occurrence of any of the following: (i) the Executive\'s conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony under the laws of the United States or any state thereof; (ii) the Executive\'s willful embezzlement or misappropriation of funds or property of the Company or any of its Affiliates in an amount exceeding Ten Thousand Dollars (\$10,000); or (iii) the Executive\'s material breach of this Agreement that is not cured by the Executive within sixty (60) calendar days ... Prior to any termination for Cause, ... A termination for Cause shall not be effective unless approved by a vote of at least two-thirds (2/3) of the members of the Board ... For the avoidance of doubt, no act or omission by the Executive shall constitute \"Cause\" if the Executive acted in good faith and with a reasonable belief that such act or omission was in or not opposed to the best interests of the Company.-]',
           '{+For purposes of this Agreement, \"Cause\" means the Executive\'s: (i) conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony or any crime involving moral turpitude, dishonesty, or fraud; (ii) willful embezzlement, misappropriation, or fraud against the Company or any of its Affiliates; (iii) gross negligence or willful misconduct in the performance of her duties that causes or is reasonably likely to cause material harm to the Company or its reputation; (iv) material breach of any fiduciary duty owed to the Company or its stockholders, including the duty of loyalty and the duty of care; (v) material breach of this Agreement or any other written agreement with the Company, including any restrictive covenant set forth herein or therein; (vi) material violation of the Company\'s Code of Business Conduct and Ethics or any other material written Company policy, including policies relating to harassment, discrimination, insider trading, and anti-corruption compliance; (vii) willful refusal to perform lawful duties as reasonably directed by the Board or the CEO; (viii) any act of dishonesty, fraud, or misrepresentation that causes or is reasonably likely to cause material harm to the Company or its reputation, whether or not such act rises to the level of a criminal offense; or (ix) any material inaccuracy in the representations and warranties set forth in Section 1.6(a).+}',
           '{+With respect to clauses (v), (vi) and (vii), if the conduct is reasonably capable of cure, Cause shall exist only if the Company has given the Executive written notice describing the conduct in reasonable detail and the Executive has failed to cure it within thirty (30) calendar days after receipt of such notice. No cure period shall apply to clauses (i), (ii), (iii), (iv), (viii) or (ix). Before a termination for Cause becomes effective, the Executive shall be given a reasonable opportunity to be heard, with counsel, before the Board. The determination of Cause shall be made by a majority of the members of the Board (excluding the Executive, if applicable). The Company may place the Executive on paid administrative leave pending such determination, and doing so shall not constitute Good Reason.+}'],
  comment='Conformed the Cause definition to the Company\'s standard for all executive officers. A 30-day cure period applies to the curable grounds, and the Executive will have an opportunity to be heard by the Board before any termination for Cause.',
  params='Negotiable: wording of the hearing right, and a \"reasonably likely to cause material harm\" qualifier on grounds (vi) and (vii). Not negotiable: all eight playbook grounds, a majority (not supermajority) vote, no monetary thresholds, no good-faith defense, and a cure period no longer than 30 days and limited to grounds (v) to (vii).'),
 dict(id='37', sec='9(b)', title='Good Reason: seven triggers including catch-all, any salary/target-bonus reduction, 25-mile relocation, travel >50%, direct reports, Board nomination; 15-business-day cure',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Severance on demand: \$2.775M draft (\$1.575M term sheet) non-CIC; \$4.16M draft (\$2.45M term sheet) CIC. Also defeats the Section 409A involuntary-separation safe harbor (see Priority Flag A)',
  draft='(i) diminution in title or duties, including reporting change or appointment of anyone with overlapping authority; (ii) any reduction in Base Salary or Target Bonus percentage, even across the board; (iii) relocation of more than 25 miles or business travel more than 50% of working days; (iv) fewer than 8 direct reports; (v) failure to nominate to the Board; (vi) material breach uncured in 15 business days; (vii) catch-all for any action affecting \"status, title, position, working conditions, benefits, or compensation.\" Cure period: 15 business days.',
  base='Playbook Section VI.D allows only: material diminution in authority, duties or responsibilities (with a CIC subsidiary carve-out); material base reduction (other than an across-the-board cut of up to 10%); relocation of more than 50 miles; and uncured material breach. Notice within 60 days, 30-day cure, resignation within 30 days after the cure period. Expressly prohibited triggers: direct reports and reporting structure, office, Board nomination, catch-alls and target-bonus reductions. The 25-mile threshold is not acceptable.',
  analysis=['Each prohibited trigger is a severance option the Executive holds. The catch-all (vii) alone would let her claim Good Reason over almost any change in \"working conditions.\" The \"appointment of any individual ... with authority ... that overlap[s]\" trigger would let her block the hiring of a Chief Supply Chain Officer or a Harmony Pet Naturals integration lead.',
           'Section 409A: a resignation for Good Reason is treated as an \"involuntary separation\" only if the definition fits the safe harbor in Treas. Reg. Section 1.409A-1(n)(2)(ii). The safe harbor requires a material negative change, notice within 90 days, a cure period of at least 30 days, and separation within 2 years. The draft\'s 15-business-day cure (about 21 days) and the catch-all fall outside it. Severance paid on a Good Reason resignation would then be nonqualified deferred compensation subject to the six-month specified-employee delay that the draft omits. Our redline satisfies the safe harbor: 60-day notice, 30-day cure, and resignation within 30 days.'],
  redline=['Section 9(b) - Good Reason. [-For purposes of this Agreement, \"Good Reason\" shall mean the occurrence of any of the following without the Executive\'s prior written consent: (i) a material diminution in the Executive\'s title, duties, authority, or responsibilities, including without limitation a change in reporting structure ... (vii) any other action or inaction by the Company that materially and adversely affects the Executive\'s status, title, position, working conditions, benefits, or compensation.-]',
           '{+For purposes of this Agreement, \"Good Reason\" means the occurrence of any of the following without the Executive\'s prior written consent: (i) a material diminution in the Executive\'s authority, duties, or responsibilities (excluding any change resulting from the Company ceasing to be a publicly traded entity or becoming a subsidiary of another entity following a Change in Control, provided such change does not otherwise materially diminish the Executive\'s authority, duties, or responsibilities with respect to the operations of the surviving or acquiring entity that were conducted by the Company immediately prior to the Change in Control); (ii) a material reduction in the Executive\'s Base Salary, other than an across-the-board reduction of not more than ten percent (10%) applicable to all similarly situated executives of the Company; (iii) a relocation of the Executive\'s principal place of employment by more than fifty (50) miles from her then-current principal place of employment; or (iv) a material breach by the Company of this Agreement. No action taken under Section 1.6(b), no placement on paid administrative leave under Section 9(a), and no recovery under the Clawback Policy shall constitute Good Reason.+}',
           'Good Reason Process. The Executive must provide written notice to the Company of the existence of the Good Reason condition within sixty (60) days of the initial existence of such condition. Such notice shall describe the Good Reason condition in reasonable detail[- and identify the specific subsection of this Section 9(b) upon which the Executive relies-]. The Company shall have [-fifteen (15) business days-]{+thirty (30) days+} from receipt of such notice to cure the condition giving rise to Good Reason{+, and if it does so, Good Reason shall be deemed not to have occurred with respect to such condition+}. If the Company fails to cure the condition within such [-fifteen (15) business day-]{+thirty (30)-day+} cure period, the Executive may resign for Good Reason by delivering a notice of resignation to the Company within thirty (30) days following the expiration of the cure period{+, failing which the Executive shall be deemed to have waived her right to resign for Good Reason with respect to such condition+}. [-A resignation for Good Reason that complies with the procedures set forth in this paragraph shall be treated as a termination by the Company without Cause for all purposes of this Agreement, including for purposes of Section 10 (Severance) and Section 11 (Change in Control).-]'],
  comment='Conformed Good Reason to the Company\'s standard executive officer definition, which tracks the Section 409A involuntary-separation safe harbor. Organizational and reporting structure, office arrangements, Board composition and incentive targets remain within the discretion of management and the Board.',
  params='Possible gives (low cost): (a) add \"removal from the position of Chief Operating Officer\" as an express example of trigger (i), since it is arguably already covered; (b) keep the draft\'s requirement that the Executive identify the subsection relied on, deleted above (it actually helps the Company). Hold: the 50-mile threshold, the 30-day cure, no catch-all, no reporting-line, direct-report, travel or target-bonus triggers, and the across-the-board exception.'),
 dict(id='38', sec='9(c); 9(d)', title='Notice periods: 30 days\' notice of without-Cause termination (pay in lieu); 60 days\' notice of resignation with pay through notice date if Company accelerates',
  sev='Low', cat=NG, impact='Up to one month of base (\$58,333 at approved base) for pay in lieu of notice. Up to two months of base if the Company waives her resignation notice',
  draft='Company must give 30 days\' notice of a without-Cause termination or pay in lieu. Executive gives 60 days\' notice of resignation; if the Company accelerates the date, it pays base through the original date.',
  base='Not addressed in the term sheet or the playbook.',
  analysis=['Both provisions are common and broadly balanced. Clarify that (a) pay in lieu of notice is not additional severance and is not stacked on the severance period, and (b) the Company\'s waiver of her resignation notice period does not convert the resignation into a termination without Cause.'],
  redline=['Section 9(c) - ... The Company may, in its sole discretion, elect to pay the Executive her Base Salary in lieu of all or any portion of the thirty (30)-day notice period and relieve the Executive of her duties during such period{+; any such payment shall be in addition to, and shall not extend, the severance period under Section 10.1+}.',
           'Section 9(d) - ... provided that the Company shall continue to pay the Executive her Base Salary through the originally specified resignation date{+, and such acceleration shall not constitute a termination by the Company without Cause or give rise to Good Reason+}.'],

sec('Section 11 - Change in Control',
 'The draft combines single-trigger vesting, a 3x multiple, a target-floor CIC bonus, PSU vesting at the greater of target or actual, 36 months of COBRA and a full Section 280G excise tax gross-up. The approved package is double-trigger vesting, a 2x multiple, 24 months of COBRA and a best-net cutback. In the context of the Harmony Pet Naturals integration and the Company\'s M&A posture, the draft structure would pay the COO to leave at closing rather than help integrate.',
 [

  draft='A four-prong definition. Prong (iii) covers mergers \"involving the Company or any of its subsidiaries.\" Incumbent Board is measured from the Effective Date.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 9.A: \"Change in Control\" has the meaning in the 2022 Plan. Playbook Section VII.A: the definition must be consistent with the Plan and Section 409A.',
  analysis=['Using the Plan definition keeps the agreement consistent with award agreements and proxy disclosure. The \"or any of its subsidiaries\" language could be argued to sweep in internal reorganizations, such as merging Harmony Pet Naturals, Inc. into another subsidiary. Because we keep the term-sheet-approved CIC lump sum, the CIC must also be a Section 409A \"change in control event\" (Treas. Reg. Section 1.409A-3(i)(5)) for the different time and form of payment to be permitted (Treas. Reg. Section 1.409A-3(c)).'],
  redline=['Section 11(a) - Definition of Change in Control.
