sec('Section 9 - Termination (Cause and Good Reason)',
 'The draft\'s Cause definition is almost impossible to satisfy, and its Good Reason definition can be triggered by routine management decisions. Taken together with the elevated severance and the absence of a release, the Company could almost never terminate her for Cause, and the Executive could almost always find a basis to resign for Good Reason and collect severance. This is the structural core of the draft and has to be rebuilt.',
 [
 dict(id='36', sec='9(a)', title='Cause limited to felony, embezzlement >\$10,000, and uncured material breach (60-day cure); 2/3 Board vote; good-faith defense',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Effectively converts misconduct terminations into without-Cause terminations: \$2.775M draft severance (\$1.575M term sheet) plus loss of signing bonus/relocation clawbacks',
  draft='Three grounds only: (i) felony conviction or plea; (ii) willful embezzlement exceeding \$10,000; (iii) material breach uncured within 60 days. Procedural overlay: specific notice, hearing before at least three independent directors, approval by two-thirds of the Board, and a blanket \"good faith\" defense.',
  base='Playbook Section VI.C requires all eight grounds: felony/moral turpitude; embezzlement/fraud; gross negligence or willful misconduct; material breach of fiduciary duty; material breach of agreement or covenants; material policy/Code violation; willful refusal to perform; and dishonesty causing harm. A 30-day cure applies only to grounds (v) to (vii). Playbook Section VI.C states that narrow definitions are \"prohibited.\"',
  analysis=['The draft omits gross negligence, willful misconduct, fiduciary breach, policy violations (harassment, insider trading, FCPA), willful refusal and dishonesty. The \$10,000 threshold would excuse smaller embezzlement. The good-faith defense borrows the DGCL Section 145 indemnification standard and would defeat Cause for almost any conduct she claims to have believed was in the Company\'s interest. The two-thirds supermajority lets a minority of directors block a Cause termination.',
           'Our redline includes one deliberate give: an opportunity to be heard before the Board, with counsel. It costs little and improves the defensibility of any Cause determination. A ninth ground covers material misrepresentation in the Meridian representations (Section 1.6).'],
  redline=['Section 9(a) - Cause. [-For purposes of this Agreement, \"Cause\" shall mean the occurrence of any of the following: (i) the Executive\'s conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony under the laws of the United States or any state thereof; (ii) the Executive\'s willful embezzlement or misappropriation of funds or property of the Company or any of its Affiliates in an amount exceeding Ten Thousand Dollars (\$10,000); or (iii) the Executive\'s material breach of this Agreement that is not cured by the Executive within sixty (60) calendar days ... Prior to any termination for Cause, ... A termination for Cause shall not be effective unless approved by a vote of at least two-thirds (2/3) of the members of the Board ... For the avoidance of doubt, no act or omission by the Executive shall constitute \"Cause\" if the Executive acted in good faith and with a reasonable belief that such act or omission was in or not opposed to the best interests of the Company.-]',
           '{+For purposes of this Agreement, \"Cause\" means the Executive\'s: (i) conviction of, or plea of guilty or nolo contendere to, a felony or any crime involving moral turpitude, dishonesty, or fraud; (ii) willful embezzlement, misappropriation, or fraud against the Company or any of its Affiliates; (iii) gross negligence or willful misconduct in the performance of her duties that causes or is reasonably likely to cause material harm to the Company or its reputation; (iv) material breach of any fiduciary duty owed to the Company or its stockholders, including the duty of loyalty and the duty of care; (v) material breach of this Agreement or any other written agreement with the Company, including any restrictive covenant set forth herein or therein; (vi) material violation of the Company\'s Code of Business Conduct and Ethics or any other material written Company policy, including policies relating to harassment, discrimination, insider trading, and anti-corruption compliance; (vii) willful refusal to perform lawful duties as reasonably directed by the Board or the CEO; (viii) any act of dishonesty, fraud, or misrepresentation that causes or is reasonably likely to cause material harm to the Company or its reputation, whether or not such act rises to the level of a criminal offense; or (ix) any material inaccuracy in the representations and warranties set forth in Section 1.6(a).+}',
           '{+With respect to clauses (v), (vi) and (vii), if the conduct is reasonably capable of cure, Cause shall exist only if the Company has given the Executive written notice describing the conduct in reasonable detail and the Executive has failed to cure it within thirty (30) calendar days after receipt of such notice. No cure period shall apply to clauses (i), (ii), (iii), (iv), (viii) or (ix). Before a termination for Cause becomes effective, the Executive shall be given a reasonable opportunity to be heard, with counsel, before the Board. The determination of Cause shall be made by a majority of the members of the Board (excluding the Executive, if applicable). The Company may place the Executive on paid administrative leave pending such determination, and doing so shall not constitute Good Reason.+}'],
  comment='Conformed the Cause definition to the Company\'s standard for all executive officers. A 30-day cure period applies to the curable grounds, and the Executive will have an opportunity to be heard by the Board before any termination for Cause.',
  params='Negotiable: wording of the hearing right, and a \"reasonably likely to cause material harm\" qualifier on grounds (vi) and (vii). Not negotiable: all eight playbook grounds, a majority (not supermajority) vote, no monetary thresholds, no good-faith defense, and a cure period no longer than 30 days and limited to grounds (v) to (vii).'),
 dict(id='37', sec='9(b)', title='Good Reason: seven triggers including catch-all, any salary/target-bonus reduction, 25-mile relocation, travel >50%, direct reports, Board nomination; 15-business-day cure',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Severance on demand: \$2.775M draft (\$1.575M term sheet) non-CIC; \$4.16M draft (\$2.45M term sheet) CIC. Also defeats the Section 409A involuntary-separation safe harbor (see Priority Flag A)',
  draft='(i) diminution in title or duties, including reporting change or appointment of anyone with overlapping authority; (ii) any reduction in Base Salary or Target Bonus percentage, even across the board; (iii) relocation of more than 25 miles or business travel more than 50% of working days; (iv) fewer than 8 direct reports; (v) failure to nominate to the Board; (vi) material breach uncured in 15 business days; (vii) catch-all for any action affecting \"status, title, position, working conditions, benefits, or compensation.\" Cure period: 15 business days.',
  base='Playbook Section VI.D allows only: material diminution in authority, duties or responsibilities (with a CIC subsidiary carve-out); material base reduction (other than an across-the-board cut of up to 10%); relocation of more than 50 miles; and uncured material breach. Notice within 60 days, 30-day cure, resignation within 30 days after the cure period. Expressly prohibited triggers: direct reports and reporting structure, office, Board nomination, catch-alls and target-bonus reductions. The 25-mile threshold is not acceptable.',
  analysis=['Each prohibited trigger is a severance option the Executive holds. The catch-all (vii) alone would let her claim Good Reason over almost any change in \"working conditions.\" The \"appointment of any individual ... with authority ... that overlap[s]\" trigger would let her block the hiring of a Chief Supply Chain Officer or a Harmony Pet Naturals integration lead.',
           'Section 409A: a resignation for Good Reason is treated as an \"involuntary separation\" only if the definition fits the safe harbor in Treas. Reg. Section 1.409A-1(n)(2)(ii). The safe harbor requires a material negative change, notice within 90 days, a cure period of at least 30 days, and separation within 2 years. The draft\'s 15-business-day cure (about 21 days) and the catch-all fall outside it. Severance paid on a Good Reason resignation would then be nonqualified deferred compensation subject to the six-month specified-employee delay that the draft omits. Our redline satisfies the safe harbor: 60-day notice, 30-day cure, and resignation within 30 days.'],
  redline=['Section 9(b) - Good Reason. [-For purposes of this Agreement, \"Good Reason\" shall mean the occurrence of any of the following without the Executive\'s prior written consent: (i) a material diminution in the Executive\'s title, duties, authority, or responsibilities, including without limitation a change in reporting structure ... (vii) any other action or inaction by the Company that materially and adversely affects the Executive\'s status, title, position, working conditions, benefits, or compensation.-]',
           '{+For purposes of this Agreement, \"Good Reason\" means the occurrence of any of the following without the Executive\'s prior written consent: (i) a material diminution in the Executive\'s authority, duties, or responsibilities (excluding any change resulting from the Company ceasing to be a publicly traded entity or becoming a subsidiary of another entity following a Change in Control, provided such change does not otherwise materially diminish the Executive\'s authority, duties, or responsibilities with respect to the operations of the surviving or acquiring entity that were conducted by the Company immediately prior to the Change in Control); (ii) a material reduction in the Executive\'s Base Salary, other than an across-the-board reduction of not more than ten percent (10%) applicable to all similarly situated executives of the Company; (iii) a relocation of the Executive\'s principal place of employment by more than fifty (50) miles from her then-current principal place of employment; or (iv) a material breach by the Company of this Agreement. No action taken under Section 1.6(b), no placement on paid administrative leave under Section 9(a), and no recovery under the Clawback Policy shall constitute Good Reason.+}',
           'Good Reason Process. The Executive must provide written notice to the Company of the existence of the Good Reason condition within sixty (60) days of the initial existence of such condition. Such notice shall describe the Good Reason condition in reasonable detail[- and identify the specific subsection of this Section 9(b) upon which the Executive relies-]. The Company shall have [-fifteen (15) business days-]{+thirty (30) days+} from receipt of such notice to cure the condition giving rise to Good Reason{+, and if it does so, Good Reason shall be deemed not to have occurred with respect to such condition+}. If the Company fails to cure the condition within such [-fifteen (15) business day-]{+thirty (30)-day+} cure period, the Executive may resign for Good Reason by delivering a notice of resignation to the Company within thirty (30) days following the expiration of the cure period{+, failing which the Executive shall be deemed to have waived her right to resign for Good Reason with respect to such condition+}. [-A resignation for Good Reason that complies with the procedures set forth in this paragraph shall be treated as a termination by the Company without Cause for all purposes of this Agreement, including for purposes of Section 10 (Severance) and Section 11 (Change in Control).-]'],
  comment='Conformed Good Reason to the Company\'s standard executive officer definition, which tracks the Section 409A involuntary-separation safe harbor. Organizational and reporting structure, office arrangements, Board composition and incentive targets remain within the discretion of management and the Board.',
  params='Possible gives (low cost): (a) add \"removal from the position of Chief Operating Officer\" as an express example of trigger (i), since it is arguably already covered; (b) keep the draft\'s requirement that the Executive identify the subsection relied on, deleted above (it actually helps the Company). Hold: the 50-mile threshold, the 30-day cure, no catch-all, no reporting-line, direct-report, travel or target-bonus triggers, and the across-the-board exception.'),
 dict(id='38', sec='9(c); 9(d)', title='Notice periods: 30 days\' notice of without-Cause termination (pay in lieu); 60 days\' notice of resignation with pay through notice date if Company accelerates',
  sev='Low', cat=NG, impact='Up to one month of base (\$58,333 at approved base) for pay in lieu of notice. Up to two months of base if the Company waives her resignation notice',
  draft='Company must give 30 days\' notice of a without-Cause termination or pay in lieu. Executive gives 60 days\' notice of resignation; if the Company accelerates the date, it pays base through the original date.',
  base='Not addressed in the term sheet or the playbook.',
  analysis=['Both provisions are common and broadly balanced. Clarify that (a) pay in lieu of notice is not additional severance and is not stacked on the severance period, and (b) the Company\'s waiver of her resignation notice period does not convert the resignation into a termination without Cause.'],
  redline=['Section 9(c) - ... The Company may, in its sole discretion, elect to pay the Executive her Base Salary in lieu of all or any portion of the thirty (30)-day notice period and relieve the Executive of her duties during such period{+; any such payment shall be in addition to, and shall not extend, the severance period under Section 10.1+}.',
           'Section 9(d) - ... provided that the Company shall continue to pay the Executive her Base Salary through the originally specified resignation date{+, and such acceleration shall not constitute a termination by the Company without Cause or give rise to Good Reason+}.'],
  comment='Clarifying changes only.',
  params='Acceptable as drafted subject to the two clarifications.'),
 dict(id='39', sec='9(e); Definitions', title='Disability definition (180 consecutive / 270 aggregate days; mutually acceptable physician)',
  sev='Low', cat=NG, impact='Delays the Company\'s ability to fill a vacant COO role. Low cost',
  draft='Disability requires 180 consecutive days or 270 days in any 12 months, certified by a mutually acceptable physician.',
  base='Not addressed.',
  analysis=['Six months is long for a COO vacancy. We recommend aligning with the LTD plan elimination period and ADA practice (for example, 120 consecutive or 180 aggregate days in 12 months). Physician selected by the Company and reasonably acceptable to the Executive.'],
  redline=['\"Disability\" means ... for a period of [-one hundred eighty (180)-]{+one hundred twenty (120)+} consecutive calendar days, or for an aggregate of [-two hundred seventy (270)-]{+one hundred eighty (180)+} calendar days in any twelve (12)-month period, as certified by a licensed physician [-mutually acceptable to the Company and-]{+selected by the Company and reasonably acceptable to+} the Executive (or the Executive\'s legal representative).'],
  comment='Aligned the Disability definition with the Company\'s long-term disability program.',
  params='Can concede the draft periods if the LTD plan uses them. Low priority.'),
 ])

sec('Section 10 - Severance',
 'Non-CIC severance is 24 months of base plus 2x target bonus, paid as a lump sum within 30 days, with no release, a target-level pro-rata bonus, 24 months of COBRA and 18 months of equity acceleration. The approved package is 18 months of base plus 1x target, paid in installments, with a release, an actual-performance pro-rata bonus, 18 months of COBRA and no equity acceleration. The cash delta alone is \$1.2M at initial rates.',
 [
 dict(id='40', sec='10.1(i)', title='Cash severance 24 months base + 2x target, lump sum within 30 days (vs. 18 months + 1x target, installments)',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='\$2,775,000 vs. \$1,575,000 = +\$1,200,000 (+76.2%) at initial rates. Year-3 draft rates: \$3,059,437.50 (+\$1,484,437.50)',
  draft='Lump sum of 24 months of base plus 2x target within 30 days (\$750,000 x 2 + \$637,500 x 2 = \$2,775,000), at then-current (escalated) rates.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 8: 18 months of base (\$1,050,000) plus 1x target (\$525,000) = \$1,575,000, paid in substantially equal installments over 18 months starting on the first payroll date after day 60, with catch-up. Playbook Sections VI.A/B and Appendix B: installments are mandatory, and 24 months plus 2x is the CEO formula.',
  analysis=['The draft gives the COO the CEO\'s severance formula. Paying a lump sum also removes the Company\'s leverage: installments let the Company stop payment if she breaches her covenants during the severance period. See Priority Flag A for the Section 409A treatment of installment severance (short-term deferral, the separation-pay exemption up to 2x the Section 401(a)(17) limit, and the six-month delay on any remaining amount).'],
  redline=['(i) Cash Severance. [-A lump-sum cash payment equal to the sum of (A) twenty-four (24) months of the Executive\'s then-current Base Salary, plus (B) two (2) times the Executive\'s then-current Target Bonus, payable within thirty (30) calendar days following the date of termination-]{+An amount equal to the sum of (A) eighteen (18) months of the Executive\'s Base Salary, plus (B) one (1) times the Executive\'s Target Bonus, in each case as in effect immediately prior to the date of termination (disregarding any reduction constituting Good Reason), payable in substantially equal installments over the eighteen (18)-month period following the date of termination in accordance with the Company\'s regular payroll schedule, commencing on the first regularly scheduled payroll date following the sixtieth (60th) day after the date of termination (with the first installment to include all amounts that would otherwise have been paid during such sixty (60)-day period), subject to Sections 10.2, 10.6 and 17+}, less all applicable federal, state, and local tax withholdings and authorized deductions. Based on the initial terms of this Agreement, such cash severance amount is [-Two Million Seven Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$2,775,000) (calculated as follows: \$750,000 x 2 = \$1,500,000, plus \$637,500 x 2 = \$1,275,000)-]{+One Million Five Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$1,575,000) (calculated as follows: \$700,000 x 1.5 = \$1,050,000, plus \$525,000 x 1 = \$525,000)+}.'],
  comment='Conformed to the Company\'s severance program for executive officers in this role: 18 months of Base Salary plus 1x Target Bonus, paid in installments and subject to the Release and continued compliance with restrictive covenants.'),
 dict(id='41', sec='10.1(ii)', title='COBRA 24 months (vs. 18), no cutoff on new employer coverage',
  sev='Medium', cat=MR, impact='+6 months of premiums (illustratively ~\$15,000 at an assumed ~\$2,500/month family premium) plus continued cost after re-employment',
  draft='24 months of full COBRA premiums (employer and employee portions), with a taxable cash alternative.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 8: 18 months, or until eligible for substantially equivalent coverage from a subsequent employer, whichever is first.',
  analysis=['COBRA coverage itself generally ends after 18 months for a termination-of-employment event. Any \"COBRA\" subsidy past 18 months is really a cash payment, which the draft partly acknowledges. The cash-equivalent fallback is sensible: it avoids nondiscrimination issues under Code Section 105(h) and the ACA for a self-insured plan. Keep it, but limit it to the approved duration and add the re-employment cutoff.'],
  redline=['... under COBRA for a period of [-twenty-four (24)-]{+eighteen (18)+} months following the date of termination {+or, if earlier, until the date on which the Executive becomes eligible for substantially equivalent group health coverage through a subsequent employer (of which the Executive shall promptly notify the Company)+} (the \"COBRA Period\"), ...'],
  comment='Conformed the COBRA subsidy to 18 months, ending on eligibility for coverage from a subsequent employer.'),
 dict(id='42', sec='10.1(iv)', title='Non-CIC equity acceleration: RSUs vesting within 18 months (incl. Make-Whole) accelerate; PSUs pro-rata on actual',
  sev='High', cat=MR, impact='Illustrative termination July 1, 2026: ~\$3.7M accelerated (\$3.2M make-whole + ~\$0.33M FY26 RSU tranche + ~\$0.17M pro-rata PSUs at target) vs. \$0',
  draft='Time-based RSUs (including the make-whole) that would vest within 18 months vest immediately. PSUs vest pro rata based on actual performance.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 8 (non-CIC severance) provides no equity acceleration. Term Sheet Section 7.B: the make-whole vests on continued employment except under the CIC provisions. Equity treatment follows the Plan and award agreements.',
  analysis=['Paired with a 12-month make-whole cliff and an easy Good Reason trigger, this clause would let the Executive resign for \"Good Reason\" in year one and keep the full \$3.2M make-whole. Action item: check the Company\'s standard PSU award agreement. If it already provides pro-rata vesting on actual performance for qualifying terminations for all executives, that treatment will apply through the award agreement in any event and does not need to appear in the employment agreement.'],
  redline=['(iv) Equity Treatment. All outstanding unvested equity awards held by the Executive (including LTI Awards and the Make-Whole Award) shall be treated in accordance with the terms of the [-applicable equity incentive plan-]{+Plan+} and {+the applicable+} individual award agreements[-; provided, however, that: (A) all time-based RSUs (including the Make-Whole Award) that would have vested within eighteen (18) months following the date of termination shall vest ...; and (B) all outstanding PSUs shall remain outstanding and eligible to vest based on actual performance ..., pro-rated for the Executive\'s period of service during such performance period. ...-].'],
  comment='Outside the change in control context, equity awards are treated as provided in the Plan and the applicable award agreements, consistent with all other executive officers.'),
 dict(id='43', sec='10.2; Exhibit A', title='No release required for severance; Exhibit A (Form of Release) \"intentionally omitted\"',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='The Company pays up to \$2.775M (draft) or \$1.575M (term sheet) and remains exposed to every employment claim (Title VII, ADEA, ADA, FMLA, contract and tort)',
  draft='\"Severance Benefits ... shall not be conditioned upon the Executive\'s execution of a general release.\" Exhibit A is omitted for the same reason.',
  base='Term Sheet Sections 8, 9 and 14: severance and CIC benefits are \"expressly conditioned\" on a timely, non-revoked general release, and this must be stated expressly. Playbook Section VI.A: mandatory, OWBPA-compliant, at least 60 days.',
  analysis=['A release is the basic bargain for severance. The Executive is 47 and covered by the ADEA, so the release must comply with the OWBPA: a 21-day consideration period (45 days in a group program), a 7-day revocation period, written advice to consult counsel, and an express reference to the ADEA. The 60-day window plus the \"later calendar year\" rule (see Section 17) avoids the Section 409A problem of the Executive controlling the year of payment.'],
  redline=['Section 10.2 - [-No Release Required. The Severance Benefits set forth in Section 10.1 shall not be conditioned upon the Executive\'s execution of a general release of claims in favor of the Company or any other person or entity. The Severance Benefits shall become payable automatically upon a Qualifying Termination, without the requirement that the Executive execute any waiver, release, or other document as a condition to receipt thereof.-]{+Release Requirement. The Executive\'s receipt of the Severance Benefits and the CIC Severance Benefits is conditioned upon the Executive\'s execution and delivery to the Company of a general release of claims in favor of the Company, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, employees, agents and successors, substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit A (the \"Release\"), and the Release becoming effective and irrevocable in accordance with its terms no later than the sixtieth (60th) day following the date of termination. If the Release does not become effective and irrevocable by such date, the Executive shall forfeit all rights to the Severance Benefits and the CIC Severance Benefits. If the period during which the Executive may consider, execute and revoke the Release begins in one calendar year and ends in the following calendar year, any payment conditioned on the Release that constitutes nonqualified deferred compensation under Section 409A shall be paid in the later calendar year.+}',
           'EXHIBIT A - FORM OF RELEASE OF CLAIMS. [-This Exhibit is intentionally omitted from this draft. The Executive\'s entitlement to Severance Benefits under Section 10 is not conditioned upon the execution of a release of claims.-]{+[Company\'s standard form of Separation Agreement and General Release to be attached. Key terms: general release of all claims through the release date (including under Title VII, the ADEA/OWBPA, the ADA, the FMLA, ERISA (other than vested benefits), the North Carolina Equal Employment Practices Act and the North Carolina Wage and Hour Act); 21-day consideration period (45 days if required) and 7-day revocation period; advice to consult counsel; reaffirmation of Sections 12, 13 and 18; customary carve-outs for vested benefits, indemnification and D&O rights, rights under this Agreement that by their terms survive, and claims that cannot be waived by law; and no prohibition on protected communications with government agencies.]+}'],
  comment='Severance is conditioned on a customary general release of claims. The Company\'s form of release is attached as Exhibit A.'),
 dict(id='44', sec='10.4', title='Death/Disability: pro-rata bonus at target floor + 12 months COBRA',
  sev='Medium', cat=MR, impact='Up to prorated target bonus (up to \$637,500) + 12 months COBRA (~\$30,000 illustrative) vs. \$0 contractual (plan benefits only)',
  draft='On death or Disability: accrued obligations, pro-rata bonus with target floor (\"calculated in the same manner\" as Section 10.1(iii)), 12 months of COBRA, and plan-based equity treatment.',
  base='Playbook Sections IV and VI.A: no pro-rata bonus or severance on death or disability; benefit plans govern. The term sheet provides none, and its Section 15 treats any added commitment as a material deviation.',
  analysis=['This is an added commitment not contemplated by the term sheet. Life insurance (3x base, capped at \$2,000,000) and supplemental LTD (60% of base) already address these events.'],
  redline=['(i) Accrued Obligations;',
           '[-(ii) a pro-rata Annual Bonus for the fiscal year in which the termination occurs, calculated in the same manner as set forth in Section 10.1(iii) and payable at the same time;-]',
           '[-(iii) the Company shall pay or reimburse the cost of continued COBRA coverage (medical, dental, and vision) for the Executive (or the Executive\'s eligible dependents) for a period of twelve (12) months following the date of termination; and-]',
           '[-(iv)-]{+(ii)+} all outstanding equity awards shall be treated in accordance with the terms of the [-applicable equity incentive plan-]{+Plan+} and individual award agreements{+; and+}',
           '{+(iii) such benefits as are provided under the Company\'s life insurance, disability and other benefit plans in accordance with their terms.+}'],
  comment='Death and disability are addressed through the Company\'s life and disability insurance programs and the equity award terms, consistent with all executive officers.'),
 dict(id='45', sec='10 (new 10.6)', title='Severance not conditioned on restrictive covenant compliance; no cessation or recoupment right',
  sev='High', cat=MR, impact='Without this, the Company keeps paying severance to an executive who is competing or soliciting. The draft compounds the problem with \"unconditional\" garden leave',
  draft='None.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 8 (Other Conditions): severance is conditioned on continued compliance with all post-termination covenants. Playbook Section VI.A: installments preserve the Company\'s remedies.',
  analysis=['Add an express condition subsequent: payments stop on a material breach, and installments already paid are recoverable (other than a nominal amount supporting the Release).'],
  redline=['{+Section 10.6 - Restrictive Covenant Compliance. The Executive\'s right to receive and retain the Severance Benefits and the CIC Severance Benefits is conditioned upon her continued compliance with Sections 12 and 13. In the event of the Executive\'s material breach of Section 12 or 13, as determined by the Company in good faith, the Company may cease providing any unpaid Severance Benefits or CIC Severance Benefits, and the Executive shall repay to the Company, upon demand, any such benefits previously paid (other than \$1,000, which shall serve as consideration for the Release), in addition to any other remedies available to the Company.+}'],
  comment='Severance remains conditioned on continued compliance with the restrictive covenants, consistent with the Company\'s program for executive officers.'),
 ])

sec('Section 11 - Change in Control',
 'The draft combines single-trigger vesting, a 3x multiple, a target-floor CIC bonus, PSU vesting at the greater of target or actual, 36 months of COBRA and a full Section 280G excise tax gross-up. The approved package is double-trigger vesting, a 2x multiple, 24 months of COBRA and a best-net cutback. In the context of the Harmony Pet Naturals integration and the Company\'s M&A posture, the draft structure would pay the COO to leave at closing rather than help integrate.',
 [
 dict(id='46', sec='11(a)', title='Bespoke Change in Control definition (not the Plan definition); captures subsidiary-level mergers; not tied to Section 409A',
  sev='Medium', cat=MR, impact='Risk of an unintended CIC trigger (for example, an internal subsidiary merger during the Harmony integration) and of Section 409A non-compliance for the CIC lump sum',
  draft='A four-prong definition. Prong (iii) covers mergers \"involving the Company or any of its subsidiaries.\" Incumbent Board is measured from the Effective Date.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 9.A: \"Change in Control\" has the meaning in the 2022 Plan. Playbook Section VII.A: the definition must be consistent with the Plan and Section 409A.',
  analysis=['Using the Plan definition keeps the agreement consistent with award agreements and proxy disclosure. The \"or any of its subsidiaries\" language could be argued to sweep in internal reorganizations, such as merging Harmony Pet Naturals, Inc. into another subsidiary. Because we keep the term-sheet-approved CIC lump sum, the CIC must also be a Section 409A \"change in control event\" (Treas. Reg. Section 1.409A-3(i)(5)) for the different time and form of payment to be permitted (Treas. Reg. Section 1.409A-3(c)).'],
  redline=['Section 11(a) - Definition of Change in Control. [-For purposes of this Agreement, a \"Change in Control\" shall mean the occurrence of any of the following events: (i) any \"person\" or \"group\" ... (iii) consummation of a merger, consolidation, statutory share exchange, or similar corporate transaction involving the Company or any of its subsidiaries ...; or (iv) the sale or other disposition of all or substantially all of the assets of the Company to any person or entity that is not an Affiliate of the Company.-]{+For purposes of this Agreement, \"Change in Control\" has the meaning set forth in the Plan; provided that, with respect to any payment hereunder that constitutes nonqualified deferred compensation subject to Section 409A and whose time or form of payment depends on the occurrence of a Change in Control, a Change in Control shall be deemed to have occurred only if the event also constitutes a \"change in control event\" within the meaning of Treasury Regulation Section 1.409A-3(i)(5). \"CIC Protection Period\" means the twenty-four (24)-month period following a Change in Control.+}'],
  comment='Conformed to the Plan definition of Change in Control (with a Section 409A overlay) so that the agreement and the equity award agreements operate consistently.'),
 dict(id='47', sec='11(b)', title='Single-trigger acceleration of all equity on a CIC (PSUs at target), regardless of termination',

  analysis=['Illustration (internal; for TJ, to be refined by the Company\'s tax advisors before any reliance). Excess parachute payment ~\$5.22M; excise tax (20%) ~\$1.04M; gross-up at a ~63.3% combined marginal rate (20% excise + 37% federal + 2.35% Medicare + 3.99% NC) ~\$2.85M.   redline=['Section 11(d) - [-Section 280G Gross-Up. In the event that any payment or benefit received or to be received by the Executive in connection with a Change in Control ... the costs of such determination shall be borne entirely by the Company.-]{+Section 280G. See Section 14.+}',
           'SECTION 14 - SECTION 280G. [-Section 14.1 - Excise Tax Gross-Up. ... Section 14.2 - Timing of Gross-Up Payment. ...-]',
           '{+Section 14.1 - Best-Net Cutback. If any payment or benefit received or to be received by the Executive, whether under this Agreement or otherwise (the \"Total Payments\"), would constitute a \"parachute payment\" within the meaning of Section 280G of the Code and would, but for this Section 14, be subject to the excise tax imposed by Section 4999 of the Code (the \"Excise Tax\"), then the Total Payments shall be reduced (but not below zero) to the extent necessary so that no portion of the Total Payments is subject to the Excise Tax, but only if the net after-tax amount of the Total Payments as so reduced (after taking into account all applicable federal, state and local income, employment and other taxes) is greater than the net after-tax amount of the unreduced Total Payments (after taking into account all such taxes and the Excise Tax). Any reduction shall be made in the following order: (1) cash severance payments, (2) accelerated vesting of equity awards, and (3) any other parachute payments, in each case in reverse chronological order of payment (the payment furthest in time from the Change in Control being reduced first), and in a manner consistent with Section 409A.+}',

In no event shall the Company be obligated to pay the Executive any gross-up, make-whole or other payment in respect of the Excise Tax or any other tax.+}'],
  comment='The Company does not provide excise tax gross-ups to any executive. Replaced with a best-net cutback, which delivers whichever result leaves the Executive with the greater after-tax amount.'),

sec('Section 12 - Restrictive Covenants',
 'The covenants are drafted to be protective in name only. The non-compete runs 6 months and covers one product category (U.S. retail household cleaning), so pet care (Harmony), personal care and specialty food are left open. The employee non-solicit covers only direct reports. There is no customer non-solicit (note the jump from 12(b) to 12(d)). The Company would also have to pay unconditional garden leave at full base salary. Under the draft\'s Minnesota choice of law (Section 15.2), even this weak non-compete would likely be void.',
 [
 dict(id='53', sec='12(a)', title='Non-compete: 6 months; household cleaning only (\"Directly Competitive Products\", U.S. retail); no stated territory',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Leaves pet care, personal care and specialty food unprotected and gives a 6-month restriction where 18/12 months is required. The value of protecting Pinnacle\'s ~\$2.3B portfolio is not quantifiable but is material',
  draft='Restricted Period: employment plus 6 months. Restricted activity is limited to \"Directly Competitive Products,\" defined as household cleaning products sold at retail in the United States that compete with the Household Cleaning segment.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 10.A: 18 months after termination for any reason, reduced to 12 months after a termination without Cause or for Good Reason. Covers all business lines (household cleaning, personal care, specialty food, pet care, including Harmony Pet Naturals and successor brands). Geography: the U.S. and any international market where the Company actively conducts business at termination. 2% passive investment exception. Playbook Section VIII.A: 12-month absolute floor; must not be limited to one product line.',
  analysis=['North Carolina enforces a non-compete that is (1) in writing, (2) part of the employment contract, (3) supported by consideration (initial employment suffices for an at-hire agreement), (4) reasonable as to time and territory, and (5) designed to protect a legitimate business interest. An 18-month period with a 12-month step-down is well within the range North Carolina courts have upheld for senior executives. A territory tied to where the Company actually does business is defensible for a COO with enterprise-wide responsibility.',
           'Enforceability caution: North Carolina applies a \"strict blue pencil\" rule. Courts may strike distinct, severable terms but will not rewrite an overbroad covenant (Hartman v. W.H. Odell & Assocs., 117 N.C. App. 307 (1994)). The North Carolina Supreme Court has held that parties cannot contract around this through a reformation clause (Beverage Sys. of the Carolinas, LLC v. Associated Beverage Repair, LLC, 368 N.C. 693 (2016)). The draft\'s Section 12(e) reformation clause therefore provides little protection. The covenant must be drafted to be enforceable as written, with business-line and territory elements set out as separable clauses (see Issue 57).'],
  redline=['Section 12(a) - Non-Competition.            '[-For purposes of this Agreement, \"Directly Competitive Products\" shall mean household cleaning products sold at retail in the United States, including without limitation surface cleaners, laundry detergents, dish soaps, disinfectants, and related household cleaning products that are competitive with the products manufactured, marketed, or distributed by the Company\'s Household Cleaning segment as of the date of the Executive\'s termination.-]',
           '{+For purposes of this Agreement: (A) \"Competing Business\" means any business, or any division, unit or segment of a business, that develops, manufactures, markets, distributes or sells products that compete with the products of any line of business conducted by the Company or any of its subsidiaries at any time during the twelve (12) months preceding the date of termination, including (1) household cleaning products, (2) personal care products, (3) specialty food products, and (4) pet care products (including the business of Harmony Pet Naturals, Inc. and any successor or related brand), each of which shall be construed as a separate and divisible restriction; and (B) \"Restricted Territory\" means (1) the United States and (2) each other country in which the Company or any of its subsidiaries actively conducts business as of the date of termination, each of which shall be construed as a separate and divisible territory.+}'],
  comment='Conformed the non-competition covenant to the Company\'s standard for executive officers: 18 months, reduced to 12 months after a termination without Cause or for Good Reason, covering each of the Company\'s product categories in the markets where the Company does business. sec('Section 15 - Dispute Resolution',
 'The draft puts all disputes in Minnesota courts, under Minnesota law, with one-way fee shifting in the Executive\'s favor. The term sheet requires AAA arbitration in Charlotte under North Carolina law, with each party bearing its own fees. The Minnesota choice of law is not just a home-court advantage: under Minn. Stat. Section 181.988 it would likely void the Company\'s non-compete outright.',
 [
 dict(id='61', sec='15.1', title='Exclusive forum: state/federal courts in Hennepin County, Minnesota (no arbitration)',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Litigation in the Executive\'s home forum, a jury, public filings. Defense costs higher than in arbitration',
  draft='Exclusive jurisdiction of Hennepin County, Minnesota courts for all claims.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 13: binding AAA arbitration under the Employment Rules, seated in Charlotte, Mecklenburg County. Playbook Section XV: single arbitrator, delegation of arbitrability, court carve-out for injunctive relief, class and collective action waiver, and jury waiver. Litigation elsewhere \"must be rejected.\"',
  analysis=['The Executive will live and work in Charlotte. Hennepin County has no connection to the employment relationship other than her current residence. Note for the arbitration clause: the Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act of 2021 (9 U.S.C. Sections 401-402) lets her elect court for sexual harassment and assault claims, so the clause should acknowledge that.'],
  redline=['Section 15.1 - [-Exclusive Forum. Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement ... shall be resolved exclusively in the state or federal courts located in Hennepin County, Minnesota. Each Party hereby irrevocably consents to the personal jurisdiction and venue of such courts ...-]{+Arbitration. Except as provided in Section 12(f) and this Section 15.1, any dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, the Executive\'s employment or the termination thereof, including the breach, termination, enforcement, interpretation or validity of this Agreement and the determination of the scope or applicability of this agreement to arbitrate, shall be resolved by final and binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association (\"AAA\") under its Employment Arbitration Rules and Mediation Procedures then in effect, before a single arbitrator experienced in executive employment matters. The seat of arbitration shall be Charlotte, Mecklenburg County, North Carolina. Either Party may seek temporary, preliminary or emergency injunctive relief in the state or federal courts located in Mecklenburg County, North Carolina, to enforce Sections 12 or 13 without waiving the right to arbitrate. To the fullest extent permitted by law, the Parties waive any right to a jury trial and agree that claims may be brought only in an individual capacity and not as a plaintiff or class member in any class, collective or representative proceeding. This Section 15.1 shall not require arbitration of any claim that, under applicable law (including 9 U.S.C. Sections 401-402), may not be the subject of a mandatory pre-dispute arbitration agreement, at the Executive\'s election.+}'],
  comment='Disputes will be resolved by AAA arbitration in Charlotte, where the Executive will be employed, with a court carve-out for injunctive relief and the statutory exception for claims that cannot be subject to mandatory arbitration.'),
 dict(id='62', sec='15.2', title='Minnesota governing law (would likely void the Company\'s non-compete under Minn. Stat. Section 181.988)',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Would likely void Section 12(a) entirely and impose Minnesota employment-law rules on a North Carolina employment relationship',
  draft='Minnesota law governs, excluding conflict-of-laws rules.',
  base='Term Sheet Sections 10.D and 13: North Carolina law governs the agreement and the restrictive covenants. Playbook Section XV: NC law, which is \"essential\" for covenant enforcement.',
  analysis=['Minn. Stat. Section 181.988, subd. 2, makes covenants not to compete in agreements entered into on or after July 1, 2023 void and unenforceable (with narrow sale-of-business and dissolution exceptions). With Minnesota law governing, the Section 12(a) non-compete would almost certainly fail. A non-compete with a 6-month period and one product category may have been drafted with that outcome in mind.',
           'Related point: subd. 3 of the statute bars requiring an employee who \"primarily resides and works in Minnesota\" to accept a non-Minnesota choice of law or forum. Once she relocates and works in Charlotte, that provision should not apply. Two steps help foreclose the argument: (a) confirm her relocation timing, including whether her family stays in Minneapolis through the school year, and (b) recite in the agreement that her principal place of employment is Charlotte from the Effective Date. Corporate-law matters (indemnification, fiduciary duties) remain governed by Delaware law.'],
  redline=['Section 15.2 - Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of [-Minnesota-]{+North Carolina+}, without giving effect to any choice of law or conflict of law principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction{+; provided that matters relating to indemnification and the internal affairs of the Company shall be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware+}. All questions concerning the construction, validity, enforcement, and interpretation of this Agreement shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of [-Minnesota-]{+North Carolina+}, without regard to the conflicts of law principles thereof. {+The Parties acknowledge that the Executive\'s principal place of employment from and after the Effective Date shall be the Company\'s principal offices in Charlotte, North Carolina.+}'],
  comment='North Carolina law governs, since the Executive will live and work in North Carolina and the Company is headquartered there. Delaware law applies to corporate governance matters.'),

sec('New Provisions to Insert (Mandatory Omissions)',
 'The draft omits two provisions that the term sheet, the playbook and (for the clawback) NYSE listing standards make mandatory. Both are discussed as Priority Flags A and B above. The full insertion text follows.',
 [
 dict(id='68', sec='New Section 17', title='PRIORITY FLAG - No Section 409A compliance provision',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Section 409A failure: income inclusion of all vested deferred amounts, a 20% additional tax and premium interest on the Executive, plus Company withholding and reporting failures and employee-relations exposure',
  draft='None. There is no savings clause, no specified-employee delay, no separate-payment designation, no separation-from-service definition and no reimbursement rules. The 75-day bonus window (Issue 20) and the gross-up timing provisions highlight the gap.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 14: 409A provisions, including (i) a six-month delay for specified employees, (ii) separate payments, and (iii) a savings clause. Playbook Section XIII: comprehensive, mandatory; omission is a \"critical compliance failure.\"',
  analysis=['See Priority Flag A for the analysis. The insertion text below follows the term sheet\'s three required elements and the playbook\'s additional requirements (separation from service, exemptions). It also adds the standard reimbursement and in-kind rules (Treas. Reg. Section 1.409A-3(i)(1)(iv)) and payment-window and release-timing protections.'],
  redline=['{+SECTION 17 - SECTION 409A+}',
           '{+(a) General. The Parties intend that the payments and benefits under this Agreement comply with, or be exempt from, Section 409A of the Code and the Treasury Regulations and other guidance issued thereunder (\"Section 409A\"), and this Agreement shall be interpreted and administered accordingly. To the extent any provision of this Agreement is ambiguous as to its compliance with Section 409A, the provision shall be read in such a manner that all payments hereunder comply with Section 409A. To the maximum extent permitted, payments hereunder are intended to qualify for the short-term deferral exception under Treasury Regulation Section 1.409A-1(b)(4) and the separation pay exception under Treasury Regulation Section 1.409A-1(b)(9)(iii).+}',
           '{+(b) Separation from Service. A termination of employment shall not be deemed to have occurred for purposes of any provision of this Agreement providing for the payment of any amount or benefit that constitutes nonqualified deferred compensation upon or following a termination of employment unless such termination is also a \"separation from service\" within the meaning of Treasury Regulation Section 1.409A-1(h), and references to a \"termination\" or \"termination of employment\" shall mean such a separation from service.+}',
           '{+(c) Specified Employee. Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, if the Executive is a \"specified employee\" (within the meaning of Treasury Regulation Section 1.409A-1(i)) on the date of her separation from service, then any payment or benefit that constitutes nonqualified deferred compensation subject to Section 409A and that is payable on account of such separation from service shall not be paid or provided before the date that is six (6) months after the date of such separation from service (or, if earlier, the date of the Executive\'s death). All payments and benefits delayed under this Section 17(c) shall be accumulated without interest and paid or provided in a lump sum on the first business day following the expiration of such period, and any remaining payments shall be paid on their original schedule.+}',
           '{+(d) Separate Payments. Each installment payment under this Agreement shall be treated as a separate payment for purposes of Section 409A, and the right to a series of installment payments shall be treated as a right to a series of separate payments.+}',
           '{+(e) Reimbursements and In-Kind Benefits. To the extent any reimbursement or in-kind benefit under this Agreement constitutes nonqualified deferred compensation, (i) the amount eligible for reimbursement or in-kind benefits in any calendar year shall not affect the amount eligible for reimbursement or in-kind benefits in any other calendar year, (ii) any reimbursement shall be made no later than the last day of the calendar year following the year in which the expense was incurred, and (iii) the right to reimbursement or in-kind benefits shall not be subject to liquidation or exchange for another benefit.+}',
           '{+(f) Payment Timing; Release Periods. Whenever a payment under this Agreement specifies a payment period with reference to a number of days, the actual date of payment within such period shall be within the sole discretion of the Company, and in no event may the Executive, directly or indirectly, designate the calendar year of any payment. The later-year rule in Section 10.2 shall apply to any payment conditioned on the Release.+}',
           '{+(g) No Acceleration or Offset. No payment of nonqualified deferred compensation under this Agreement may be accelerated or offset except as permitted by Treasury Regulation Section 1.409A-3(j)(4).+}',
           '{+(h) No Guarantee. Although the Company intends to administer this Agreement in compliance with Section 409A, the Company makes no representation or warranty that the payments and benefits hereunder will comply with or be exempt from Section 409A, and in no event shall the Company be liable for any tax, interest or penalty that may be imposed on the Executive under Section 409A or for any damages for failing to comply with Section 409A.+}'],
