sec('Section 12 - Restrictive Covenants',
 'The covenants are drafted to be protective in name only. The non-compete runs 6 months and covers one product category (U.S. retail household cleaning), so pet care (Harmony), personal care and specialty food are left open. The employee non-solicit covers only direct reports. There is no customer non-solicit (note the jump from 12(b) to 12(d)). The Company would also have to pay unconditional garden leave at full base salary. Under the draft\'s Minnesota choice of law (Section 15.2), even this weak non-compete would likely be void.',
 [
 dict(id='53', sec='12(a)', title='Non-compete: 6 months; household cleaning only (\"Directly Competitive Products\", U.S. retail); no stated territory',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Leaves pet care, personal care and specialty food unprotected and gives a 6-month restriction where 18/12 months is required. The value of protecting Pinnacle\'s ~\$2.3B portfolio is not quantifiable but is material',
  draft='Restricted Period: employment plus 6 months. Restricted activity is limited to \"Directly Competitive Products,\" defined as household cleaning products sold at retail in the United States that compete with the Household Cleaning segment.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 10.A: 18 months after termination for any reason, reduced to 12 months after a termination without Cause or for Good Reason. Covers all business lines (household cleaning, personal care, specialty food, pet care, including Harmony Pet Naturals and successor brands). Geography: the U.S. and any international market where the Company actively conducts business at termination. 2% passive investment exception. Playbook Section VIII.A: 12-month absolute floor; must not be limited to one product line.',
  analysis=['North Carolina enforces a non-compete that is (1) in writing, (2) part of the employment contract, (3) supported by consideration (initial employment suffices for an at-hire agreement), (4) reasonable as to time and territory, and (5) designed to protect a legitimate business interest. An 18-month period with a 12-month step-down is well within the range North Carolina courts have upheld for senior executives. A territory tied to where the Company actually does business is defensible for a COO with enterprise-wide responsibility.',
           'Enforceability caution: North Carolina applies a \"strict blue pencil\" rule. Courts may strike distinct, severable terms but will not rewrite an overbroad covenant (Hartman v. W.H. Odell & Assocs., 117 N.C. App. 307 (1994)). The North Carolina Supreme Court has held that parties cannot contract around this through a reformation clause (Beverage Sys. of the Carolinas, LLC v. Associated Beverage Repair, LLC, 368 N.C. 693 (2016)). The draft\'s Section 12(e) reformation clause therefore provides little protection. The covenant must be drafted to be enforceable as written, with business-line and territory elements set out as separable clauses (see Issue 57).'],
  redline=['Section 12(a) - Non-Competition. During the Executive\'s employment with the Company and for a period of [-six (6) months following the termination of the Executive\'s employment for any reason (the \"Restricted Period\")-]{+eighteen (18) months following the termination of the Executive\'s employment for any reason; provided that if the Executive\'s employment is terminated by the Company without Cause or by the Executive for Good Reason, such period shall be twelve (12) months following the date of termination (the \"Non-Compete Period\")+}, the Executive shall not, directly or indirectly, ... {+within the Restricted Territory,+} (i) engage in, be employed by, consult for, or render services to any [-business, person, or entity that develops, manufactures, markets, distributes, or sells Directly Competitive Products-]{+Competing Business+}; (ii) own, manage, operate, control, or participate in the ownership, management, operation, or control of any [-business, person, or entity that develops, manufactures, markets, distributes, or sells Directly Competitive Products-]{+Competing Business+}; or (iii) assist any person or entity in doing any of the foregoing; ...',
           '[-For purposes of this Agreement, \"Directly Competitive Products\" shall mean household cleaning products sold at retail in the United States, including without limitation surface cleaners, laundry detergents, dish soaps, disinfectants, and related household cleaning products that are competitive with the products manufactured, marketed, or distributed by the Company\'s Household Cleaning segment as of the date of the Executive\'s termination.-]',
           '{+For purposes of this Agreement: (A) \"Competing Business\" means any business, or any division, unit or segment of a business, that develops, manufactures, markets, distributes or sells products that compete with the products of any line of business conducted by the Company or any of its subsidiaries at any time during the twelve (12) months preceding the date of termination, including (1) household cleaning products, (2) personal care products, (3) specialty food products, and (4) pet care products (including the business of Harmony Pet Naturals, Inc. and any successor or related brand), each of which shall be construed as a separate and divisible restriction; and (B) \"Restricted Territory\" means (1) the United States and (2) each other country in which the Company or any of its subsidiaries actively conducts business as of the date of termination, each of which shall be construed as a separate and divisible territory.+}'],
  comment='Conformed the non-competition covenant to the Company\'s standard for executive officers: 18 months, reduced to 12 months after a termination without Cause or for Good Reason, covering each of the Company\'s product categories in the markets where the Company does business. As COO, the Executive will have enterprise-wide responsibility and access to confidential information across all business lines.'),
 dict(id='54', sec='12(b)', title='Employee non-solicit: 6 months; former direct reports only',
  sev='High', cat=MR, impact='Leaves ~6,800 employees outside the Executive\'s direct reports unprotected after her departure, and makes the protection very short',
  draft='Restricted Period (6 months). Covers only people who were her direct reports in the prior 12 months. General-advertising carve-out.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 10.B: 18 months, reduced to 12 after a qualifying termination; covers any employee of the Company or its subsidiaries, regardless of reporting line. Playbook Section VIII.B: all employees, with a general-advertising carve-out.',
  analysis=['A COO has visibility into talent across the organization, including the plant, supply chain and quality leadership in all four segments. A direct-reports-only restriction is materially insufficient. Keep the general-advertising carve-out, which the playbook permits.'],
  redline=['Section 12(b) - Non-Solicitation of Employees. During the [-Restricted Period-]{+Executive\'s employment and for eighteen (18) months following the termination of the Executive\'s employment for any reason (or twelve (12) months if the Executive\'s employment is terminated by the Company without Cause or by the Executive for Good Reason) (the \"Non-Solicit Period\")+}, the Executive shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit, recruit, hire, or attempt to solicit, recruit, or hire any individual who [-was a direct report to the Executive at any time during the twelve (12)-month period preceding the termination of the Executive\'s employment-]{+is an employee of the Company or any of its subsidiaries, regardless of whether such employee reports directly to the Executive+}, or encourage, induce, or attempt to encourage or induce any such individual to leave the employ of the Company or any of its Affiliates{+, or assist any other person or entity in doing any of the foregoing+}. ...'],
  comment='Conformed to the Company\'s standard employee non-solicitation covenant, which covers all employees given the COO\'s organization-wide role. The general advertising carve-out is retained.'),
 dict(id='55', sec='12(c) (missing)', title='No customer/business-relationship non-solicit (draft skips from 12(b) to 12(d))',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Customer, retailer, co-manufacturer and supplier relationships are unprotected after departure',
  draft='None. The section numbering skips 12(c).',
  base='Term Sheet Section 10.C: 18 months, reduced to 12, covering customers, clients, vendors, suppliers and business partners. Playbook Section VIII.B: mandatory, and an agreement without it is \"non-compliant.\" The playbook scope is limited to relationships with material contact or confidential information in the 12 months before termination.',
  analysis=['The gap in the lettering suggests the clause was deliberately removed. For a COO responsible for procurement, co-manufacturing and distribution, supplier and vendor relationships are as important as retail customer relationships.',
           'Scope choice: the term sheet\'s formulation (\"any customer ... or business partner\") is broader than the playbook\'s \"material contact or Confidential Information\" formulation. Given North Carolina\'s strict blue-pencil rule, we recommend the playbook\'s narrower scope, which North Carolina courts more readily enforce. That keeps the term sheet\'s duration and categories while improving enforceability.'],
  redline=['{+Section 12(c) - Non-Solicitation of Customers and Business Relationships. During the Non-Solicit Period, the Executive shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit, divert, or take away, or attempt to solicit, divert, or take away, the business or patronage of any customer, client, supplier, vendor, distributor, co-manufacturer or other business partner of the Company or any of its subsidiaries with whom the Executive had material contact, or about whom the Executive obtained Confidential Information, during the twelve (12) months preceding the date of termination, for the purpose of providing products or services competitive with those of the Company or of inducing such person to cease or adversely modify its business relationship with the Company or any of its subsidiaries.+}'],
  comment='Added the Company\'s standard customer and business-relationship non-solicitation covenant, limited to relationships with which the Executive had material contact or about which she obtained confidential information.'),
 dict(id='56', sec='12(d)', title='Garden leave at full base salary during the Restricted Period, unconditional, in addition to severance',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='+\$375,000 (6 months at \$750,000) to \$413,437.50 (year-3 rates), paid even if she breaches. Drafting defect could double-pay salary during employment',
  draft='Full base salary during the Restricted Period as \"garden leave,\" on top of severance, \"unconditional\" even if the Executive breaches the covenants.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 10.A: no separate garden leave compensation; covenant consideration is embedded in severance. Playbook Section VIII.A: garden leave is not permitted and must be struck.',
  analysis=['North Carolina requires no separate payment. Initial employment is sufficient consideration for an at-hire covenant. Paying the Executive during a period in which she is competing would be anomalous.',
           'Drafting defect: \"Restricted Period\" is defined in Section 12(a) to include the period of employment, so Section 12(d) literally entitles her to a second full base salary while employed. That alone would cost \$750,000 a year. The clause must be deleted in full.'],
  redline=['Section 12(d) - [-Garden Leave Compensation. During the Restricted Period, the Company shall continue to pay the Executive her full Base Salary ... as \"garden leave\" compensation, ... Such garden leave payments shall be in addition to, and shall not offset or reduce, any severance, equity, bonus, or other payments ... The Company\'s obligation to make garden leave payments under this Section 12(d) shall be unconditional and shall not be subject to the Executive\'s compliance with the restrictive covenants set forth in this Section 12 ...-]{+No Additional Consideration. The Executive acknowledges that her employment, the compensation and benefits provided under this Agreement (including the Signing Bonus, the Make-Whole Award and eligibility for the Severance Benefits and CIC Severance Benefits) constitute full and adequate consideration for the covenants in this Section 12, and that no garden leave or other payment shall be due in respect of any restricted period.+}'],
  comment='The covenants are supported by the Executive\'s employment and her compensation package, including severance eligibility. Separate garden leave pay is not part of the Company\'s program.'),
 dict(id='57', sec='12(e); 12(f)', title='Reformation clause of limited value under NC law; add divisibility, notice and tolling mechanics',
  sev='Medium', cat=MR, impact='Enforceability. Determines whether any covenant survives a challenge',
  draft='12(e): judicial reformation. 12(f): injunctive relief without bond and tolling during breach.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 10.D: NC law; severability providing that an unenforceable provision \"shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary.\" Playbook Section XV: a court carve-out for injunctive relief in Mecklenburg County.',
  analysis=['Keep the reformation language, because it may help if a court outside North Carolina hears the matter. Add express divisibility, which is the tool North Carolina courts will actually use. Also add a court carve-out for injunctive relief that works with the arbitration clause, and a duty to disclose the covenants to future employers.'],
  redline=['Section 12(e) - ... and such restriction, as so reformed, shall be binding upon the Parties. {+The covenants in Sections 12(a), (b) and (c), and each separately enumerated product category and territory within the definitions of Competing Business and Restricted Territory, are separate and divisible covenants, and if any of them is held unenforceable the remainder shall be enforced to the fullest extent permitted. The existence of any claim by the Executive against the Company shall not constitute a defense to enforcement of this Section 12.+}',
           'Section 12(f) - ... the Restricted Period shall be tolled during the period of such breach{+, to the extent permitted by applicable law. Notwithstanding Section 15, the Company may seek such relief in the state or federal courts located in Mecklenburg County, North Carolina. During the Non-Compete Period and Non-Solicit Period, the Executive shall provide a copy of this Section 12 to any prospective employer or business partner before accepting employment or engagement, and the Company may do so as well+}.'],
  comment='Added divisibility and procedural provisions to support enforcement of the covenants as written.'),
 ])

sec('Section 13 - Intellectual Property and Confidentiality',
 'Despite its heading, Section 13 contains no assignment of intellectual property. The confidentiality carve-outs are also overbroad, in particular the carve-out for \"general knowledge, skills, and experience ... acquired during ... employment.\" The DTSA notice is compliant.',
 [
 dict(id='58', sec='13(a) (Carve-Out)', title='Overbroad confidentiality carve-outs: prior knowledge and unqualified \"general knowledge, skills and experience\" acquired at Pinnacle',
  sev='High', cat=MR, impact='Could permit use of formulations, manufacturing processes and pricing learned at Pinnacle',
  draft='Excludes information (ii) known to the Executive before disclosure, as shown by her records, (iii) received from a third party not \"to the Executive\'s knowledge\" bound by confidentiality, and (iv) her \"general knowledge, skills, and experience, including ... acquired during the course of the Executive\'s employment with the Company.\"',
  base='Playbook Section IX.A permits only: public information, information from third parties not under confidentiality obligations, legally compelled disclosure (with notice) and DTSA disclosures. A general-skills carve-out must be narrowly drafted using the standard language. Term Sheet Section 14: confidentiality survives in perpetuity.',
  analysis=['Carve-out (iv) is the most dangerous. For an executive with a Ph.D. in chemical engineering who will oversee product formulation and manufacturing, almost any process know-how could be described as \"general knowledge ... acquired during employment.\" Carve-out (ii) would also cover information she brings from Meridian, which conflicts with the Section 1.6 representations.'],
  redline=['Carve-Out. Notwithstanding the foregoing, \"Confidential Information\" shall not include information that: (i) is or becomes publicly available through no fault, act, or omission of the Executive{+ and other than as a result of a breach of the Executive\'s obligations hereunder+}; {+or+} [-(ii) was lawfully known to the Executive prior to its disclosure by the Company, as evidenced by the Executive\'s contemporaneous written records; (iii)-]{+(ii)+} is lawfully received by the Executive from a third party who is not[-, to the Executive\'s knowledge,-] subject to any obligation of confidentiality with respect to such information[-; or (iv) constitutes the Executive\'s general knowledge, skills, and experience, including knowledge, skills, and experience acquired during the course of the Executive\'s employment with the Company-]. {+Nothing herein shall prevent the Executive from using general professional knowledge, skills, and experience that do not constitute Confidential Information as defined herein.+}'],
  comment='Conformed the carve-outs to the Company\'s standard confidentiality provisions. The Executive\'s general professional skills remain unrestricted to the extent they do not involve Confidential Information.'),
 dict(id='59', sec='13 (new 13(d))', title='No inventions/work-product assignment clause',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Company ownership of formulations, process improvements and other IP developed by the COO depends on default rules (work for hire and the hired-to-invent or shop-right doctrines), which give incomplete protection, especially for patentable inventions',
  draft='None, despite the section heading.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 14: customary inventions assignment consistent with the Company\'s standard IP Assignment Agreement for senior executives. Playbook Section IX.B: mandatory, \"critical gap\" if omitted. It covers inventions relating to the business, made with Company resources, or resulting from duties, with a carve-out for own-time inventions.',
  analysis=['Copyright work-for-hire rules do not cover patentable inventions. Without a present assignment (\"hereby assigns\"), the Company would be left with an implied-assignment or shop-right argument. North Carolina\'s statute, N.C. Gen. Stat. Section 66-57.1, makes unenforceable any assignment of inventions developed entirely on the employee\'s own time without Company resources that do not relate to the business or result from her work. Our carve-out tracks it.'],
  redline=['{+Section 13(d) - Inventions and Work Product. (i) The Executive hereby assigns, and agrees to assign, to the Company all right, title and interest in and to all inventions, discoveries, improvements, formulations, processes, innovations, works of authorship, designs, trade secrets and other intellectual property (\"Inventions\") conceived, developed, created or reduced to practice by the Executive, alone or jointly, during her employment that (A) relate to the actual or demonstrably anticipated business, research or development of the Company or any of its subsidiaries, (B) are developed using the Company\'s equipment, supplies, facilities, resources or Confidential Information, or (C) result from work performed by the Executive for the Company. All copyrightable Inventions shall be \"works made for hire\" to the extent permitted by law. (ii) This Section 13(d) does not apply to any Invention that the Executive developed entirely on her own time without using the Company\'s equipment, supplies, facilities, resources or Confidential Information and that neither relates to the Company\'s business or actual or demonstrably anticipated research or development nor results from work performed by the Executive for the Company, consistent with N.C. Gen. Stat. Section 66-57.1. (iii) The Executive shall promptly disclose all Inventions to the Company and, during and after her employment, execute all documents and take all actions reasonably requested to perfect, register and enforce the Company\'s rights, at the Company\'s expense, and hereby irrevocably appoints the Company as her attorney-in-fact for such purpose. (iv) Concurrently with this Agreement, the Executive shall execute the Company\'s standard Intellectual Property Assignment Agreement for senior executives, which shall be read together with this Section 13(d).+}'],
  comment='Added the Company\'s standard inventions and work-product assignment, including the statutory carve-out for inventions developed entirely on the Executive\'s own time.'),
 dict(id='60', sec='13 (new 13(e))', title='No protected-activity (whistleblower) carve-out',
  sev='Medium', cat=MR, impact='Regulatory exposure: SEC Rule 21F-17 enforcement actions have targeted confidentiality and release language that impedes reporting',
  draft='The DTSA notice is present (and compliant), but there is no general carve-out for communications with government agencies.',
  base='Playbook Section IX.A requires the DTSA notice. The protected-activity carve-out is recommended as a compliance matter (not addressed in the term sheet).',
  analysis=['The SEC has repeatedly brought Rule 21F-17 actions against issuers whose employment agreements or releases could be read to restrict reporting. The carve-out protects the Company and the enforceability of Section 13, and it costs nothing.'],
  redline=['{+Section 13(e) - Protected Activity. Nothing in this Agreement or in any other agreement or Company policy prohibits or restricts the Executive from filing a charge or complaint with, communicating with, providing information to, or participating in any investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission or any other federal, state or local governmental agency, or from receiving an award for information provided to any governmental agency, in each case without notice to the Company.+}'],
  comment='Added a customary protected-activity provision consistent with SEC rules.'),
 ])

sec('Section 15 - Dispute Resolution',
 'The draft puts all disputes in Minnesota courts, under Minnesota law, with one-way fee shifting in the Executive\'s favor. The term sheet requires AAA arbitration in Charlotte under North Carolina law, with each party bearing its own fees. The Minnesota choice of law is not just a home-court advantage: under Minn. Stat. Section 181.988 it would likely void the Company\'s non-compete outright.',
 [
 dict(id='61', sec='15.1', title='Exclusive forum: state/federal courts in Hennepin County, Minnesota (no arbitration)',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Litigation in the Executive\'s home forum, a jury, public filings. Defense costs higher than in arbitration',
  draft='Exclusive jurisdiction of Hennepin County, Minnesota courts for all claims.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 13: binding AAA arbitration under the Employment Rules, seated in Charlotte, Mecklenburg County. Playbook Section XV: single arbitrator, delegation of arbitrability, court carve-out for injunctive relief, class and collective action waiver, and jury waiver. Litigation elsewhere \"must be rejected.\"',
  analysis=['The Executive will live and work in Charlotte. Hennepin County has no connection to the employment relationship other than her current residence. Note for the arbitration clause: the Ending Forced Arbitration of Sexual Assault and Sexual Harassment Act of 2021 (9 U.S.C. Sections 401-402) lets her elect court for sexual harassment and assault claims, so the clause should acknowledge that.'],
  redline=['Section 15.1 - [-Exclusive Forum. Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement ... shall be resolved exclusively in the state or federal courts located in Hennepin County, Minnesota. Each Party hereby irrevocably consents to the personal jurisdiction and venue of such courts ...-]{+Arbitration. Except as provided in Section 12(f) and this Section 15.1, any dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, the Executive\'s employment or the termination thereof, including the breach, termination, enforcement, interpretation or validity of this Agreement and the determination of the scope or applicability of this agreement to arbitrate, shall be resolved by final and binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association (\"AAA\") under its Employment Arbitration Rules and Mediation Procedures then in effect, before a single arbitrator experienced in executive employment matters. The seat of arbitration shall be Charlotte, Mecklenburg County, North Carolina. Either Party may seek temporary, preliminary or emergency injunctive relief in the state or federal courts located in Mecklenburg County, North Carolina, to enforce Sections 12 or 13 without waiving the right to arbitrate. To the fullest extent permitted by law, the Parties waive any right to a jury trial and agree that claims may be brought only in an individual capacity and not as a plaintiff or class member in any class, collective or representative proceeding. This Section 15.1 shall not require arbitration of any claim that, under applicable law (including 9 U.S.C. Sections 401-402), may not be the subject of a mandatory pre-dispute arbitration agreement, at the Executive\'s election.+}'],
  comment='Disputes will be resolved by AAA arbitration in Charlotte, where the Executive will be employed, with a court carve-out for injunctive relief and the statutory exception for claims that cannot be subject to mandatory arbitration.'),
 dict(id='62', sec='15.2', title='Minnesota governing law (would likely void the Company\'s non-compete under Minn. Stat. Section 181.988)',
  sev='Critical', cat=MR, impact='Would likely void Section 12(a) entirely and impose Minnesota employment-law rules on a North Carolina employment relationship',
  draft='Minnesota law governs, excluding conflict-of-laws rules.',
  base='Term Sheet Sections 10.D and 13: North Carolina law governs the agreement and the restrictive covenants. Playbook Section XV: NC law, which is \"essential\" for covenant enforcement.',
  analysis=['Minn. Stat. Section 181.988, subd. 2, makes covenants not to compete in agreements entered into on or after July 1, 2023 void and unenforceable (with narrow sale-of-business and dissolution exceptions). With Minnesota law governing, the Section 12(a) non-compete would almost certainly fail. A non-compete with a 6-month period and one product category may have been drafted with that outcome in mind.',
           'Related point: subd. 3 of the statute bars requiring an employee who \"primarily resides and works in Minnesota\" to accept a non-Minnesota choice of law or forum. Once she relocates and works in Charlotte, that provision should not apply. Two steps help foreclose the argument: (a) confirm her relocation timing, including whether her family stays in Minneapolis through the school year, and (b) recite in the agreement that her principal place of employment is Charlotte from the Effective Date. Corporate-law matters (indemnification, fiduciary duties) remain governed by Delaware law.'],
  redline=['Section 15.2 - Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of [-Minnesota-]{+North Carolina+}, without giving effect to any choice of law or conflict of law principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction{+; provided that matters relating to indemnification and the internal affairs of the Company shall be governed by the laws of the State of Delaware+}. All questions concerning the construction, validity, enforcement, and interpretation of this Agreement shall be governed by the internal laws of the State of [-Minnesota-]{+North Carolina+}, without regard to the conflicts of law principles thereof. {+The Parties acknowledge that the Executive\'s principal place of employment from and after the Effective Date shall be the Company\'s principal offices in Charlotte, North Carolina.+}'],
  comment='North Carolina law governs, since the Executive will live and work in North Carolina and the Company is headquartered there. Delaware law applies to corporate governance matters.'),
 dict(id='63', sec='15.3', title='One-sided fee shifting: Company pays Executive\'s fees if she prevails on \"any material claim\"',
  sev='High', cat=MR, impact='Uncapped. Funds litigation against the Company. Partial success on one claim shifts all of her fees',
  draft='The Company reimburses all of the Executive\'s fees if she prevails on any material claim. If the Company wins, each side bears its own fees.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 13: each party bears its own fees and costs except as otherwise required by law; arbitrator costs shared equally. Playbook Section XV: one-sided fee shifting is \"not acceptable.\" Mutual prevailing-party clauses only with Committee and GC approval.',
  analysis=['The asymmetry encourages marginal claims, such as challenges to bonus determinations under Section 5.4. Note on arbitrator fees: the AAA treats individually negotiated executive agreements differently from employer-promulgated plans, so equal sharing is generally permitted where the executive is represented by counsel, as here. Retain the \"except as required by applicable law\" qualifier.'],
  redline=['Section 15.3 - Attorneys\' Fees. [-In the event of any dispute, controversy, litigation, or legal proceeding between the Parties ..., if the Executive prevails on any material claim asserted by or against the Executive in such proceeding, the Company shall reimburse the Executive for all reasonable attorneys\' fees, costs, disbursements, and expenses incurred by the Executive in connection with such dispute ... The determination of whether the Executive has \"prevailed on any material claim\" shall be made by the court or other decision-maker resolving such dispute.-]{+Each Party shall bear its own attorneys\' fees, costs and expenses in connection with any arbitration or other proceeding arising under or relating to this Agreement or the Executive\'s employment, except as otherwise required by applicable law. The fees and costs of the arbitrator and the AAA shall be shared equally by the Parties, except as otherwise required by applicable law.+}'],
  comment='Each party bears its own fees, with arbitrator costs shared, which is the Company\'s standard for all executive officers.',
  params='Fallback only with Comp Committee and GC approval: a MUTUAL prevailing-party clause limited to claims under this Agreement. Do not offer it unprompted.'),
 ])

sec('Section 16 - Miscellaneous; Signature Page; Exhibits',
 'These are mostly conforming changes. The main substantive point is replacing the bespoke indemnity with the Company\'s standard Indemnification Agreement and adding the statutory prohibition on indemnifying clawed-back amounts.',
 [
 dict(id='64', sec='16.1', title='Bespoke indemnification (broader than standard; no clawback carve-out)',
  sev='Medium', cat=MR, impact='Advancement and indemnity broader than for other officers. Could be read to cover clawback recoveries, which Rule 10D-1 prohibits',
  draft='Indemnify \"from and against any and all claims ... arising out of or relating to the Executive\'s employment,\" with mandatory advancement.',
  base='Term Sheet Section 11: D&O indemnification consistent with other executive officers, including advancement. Playbook Section XVI: reference the standard Indemnification Agreement, not bespoke terms. Clawback Policy Summary Section 6: the Company is prohibited from indemnifying clawed-back amounts (Rule 10D-1(b)(1)(v)).',
  analysis=['\"Arising out of or relating to the Executive\'s employment\" is broad enough to cover claims the Company itself brings, or amounts recovered under the Clawback Policy. Use the standard Indemnification Agreement for parity across officers.'],
  redline=['Section 16.1 - Indemnification. [-The Company shall indemnify and hold harmless the Executive to the fullest extent permitted by the laws of the State of Delaware ... from and against any and all claims, damages, losses, liabilities ... arising out of or relating to the Executive\'s employment with the Company, ... The Company\'s obligations under this Section 16.1 shall survive the termination of the Executive\'s employment for any reason.-]{+The Executive shall be entitled to indemnification and advancement of expenses to the fullest extent permitted by the Delaware General Corporation Law and the Company\'s Amended and Restated Certificate of Incorporation and Amended and Restated Bylaws, as in effect from time to time, and the Company and the Executive shall enter into the Company\'s standard form of Indemnification Agreement for executive officers concurrently with the execution of this Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing or anything in any other agreement, the Company shall not indemnify, insure or reimburse the Executive for the loss of any compensation recovered pursuant to the Clawback Policy.+}'],
  comment='Indemnification will be provided under the Company\'s standard Indemnification Agreement, on the same terms as for all other executive officers, subject to the clawback rules under federal securities law.'),
 dict(id='65', sec='16.3; 16.11; 16.7', title='Entire agreement, survival and notice conforming changes; notice-party name discrepancy',
  sev='Low', cat=MR, impact='Conforming',
  draft='Entire agreement does not reference the Indemnification Agreement, IP Agreement or Clawback Policy. Survival omits the new sections. Notice copy to \"Margaret Hu, Esq.\" at mhu@hucalloway.com.',

  redline=['Section 16.3 - This Agreement, together with {+the Indemnification Agreement, the Intellectual Property Assignment Agreement, the Clawback Policy and acknowledgment thereof, the Plan and+} any equity award agreements[-, the Company\'s equity incentive plan(s),-] and the Company\'s benefit plans referenced herein, constitutes the entire agreement ...',
           'Section 16.7 - If to the Company: ... Attention: Thomas \"TJ\" Jeffords, General Counsel ... {+With a copy (which shall not constitute notice) to: Redmond, Pace & Varela LLP, 227 West Trade Street, Suite 3400, Charlotte, NC 28202, Attention: Elise Varela.+} ... With a copy (which shall not constitute notice) to: Margaret [-Hu-]{+[Hsu/Hu - confirm]+}, Esq. Hu & Calloway LLP ...',

 dict(id='66', sec='Signature page', title='Board Chair \"acknowledgment\" signature block confirming \"the Board\'s authorization\"',

 dict(id='67', sec='Exhibit B', title='Equity summary table reflects non-conforming terms',

**Draft Executive Employment Agreement --- Dr. Vanessa Okafor-Chen, Chief Operating Officer\
Pinnacle Consumer Brands, Inc. (NYSE: PCBI)**

  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **TO:**                             Thomas "TJ" Jeffords, General Counsel; Kendra Millstone, Chief Human Resources Officer --- Pinnacle Consumer Brands, Inc.

  **CC:**                             Elise Varela, Partner

  **DATE:**                           October 9, 2025 (draft for partner review; client delivery October 10, 2025)

  **MATTER:**                         Pinnacle Consumer Brands, Inc. / Executive Hiring --- Okafor-Chen

  **RE:**                             Section-by-section markup of the draft Executive Employment Agreement for Dr. Vanessa Okafor-Chen (Chief Operating Officer), Hu & Calloway LLP draft dated October 3, 2025, measured against the Compensation Committee-approved Term Sheet (September 18, 2025), the Executive Compensation Playbook (v4.2, July 2025) and the Incentive-Based Compensation Clawback Policy (adopted November 15, 2023)
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# How to Use This Document

Part I gives the bottom line. Part II is the summary table of every deviation (issue, section, severity, category and financial impact). Part III quantifies the aggregate financial exposure. Part IV covers the three priority flags you asked us to highlight: Section 409A, the Dodd-Frank clawback and the Meridian non-compete. Part V walks through the draft section by section. Each issue gives the draft provision, the approved baseline (Term Sheet and Playbook), our analysis, the severity and category, and proposed redline language. Part VI is the negotiation map, Part VII lists document discrepancies and open action items, and the Appendix sets out calculation assumptions.

The proposed redlines in Part V are inserted as genuine Word tracked changes (author: Redmond, Pace & Varela LLP). Deletions appear as struck text and insertions as underlined text, and they can be accepted into a counter-draft directly. An ellipsis (...) marks unchanged draft text omitted for brevity. Each redline also carries a Word margin comment. The margin comments are written to be safe for external use: they do not refer to the Playbook or the internal Term Sheet and may be carried into the counter-draft sent to Hu & Calloway. All other text in this document is privileged, internal analysis and must not be shared with the Executive or her counsel.

Severity scale:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Rating**                          **Meaning**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Critical**                        Legal/regulatory compliance failure, governance defect, or exposure over \$1M or uncapped. Must be resolved before signing.

  High                                Material economic deviation (roughly \$100K to \$1M) or significant erosion of Company protection.

  Medium                              Moderate cost (under \~\$100K) or a remediable protective or technical gap.

  Low                                 Drafting, conforming or policy-alignment point with minimal cost.
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Categories: Must-Reject = non-negotiable because it violates the Committee-approved Term Sheet, the Playbook or applicable law. Negotiable = room for give-and-take within the stated parameters, which never exceed the Term Sheet economics.

# Part I --- Executive Summary

**Bottom line.**

The Hu & Calloway draft cannot be signed in anything like its current form. We identified 70 deviations from the approved Term Sheet and the Playbook: 19 Critical, 19 High, 17 Medium and 15 Low. 59 of them are must-reject items (non-negotiable because they breach the Committee-approved economics, the Playbook or applicable law). Only 11 are potentially negotiable, and each of those has specific parameters set out below. Because TJ has instructed that we will not go back to the Compensation Committee, the Term Sheet is a hard ceiling on economics. Every provision that adds cost, changes the structure or duration of severance or CIC benefits, weakens a restrictive covenant or adds an unapproved commitment is a "material deviation" under Term Sheet Section 15 and has to come out.

**What the draft would cost.**

Year-1 target total direct compensation rises from \$2,725,000 to \$3,387,500 (+\$662,500, +24.3%). Over the three-year Initial Term, at target performance, the recurring deltas (base and escalator, target bonus, LTI, perquisites and the relocation cap) total \$2,300,685.53. At maximum bonus payout the total is \$3,526,500.17. On top of that, the draft guarantees \$637,500 of bonus for FY2026 and FY2027 regardless of performance. The event-driven exposure is larger still. A without-Cause or Good Reason termination in year 1 would cost about \$5,290,000 more than the Term Sheet. A Change in Control followed by termination would cost about \$5,944,315.07 more, including an estimated \~\$2.85M Section 280G gross-up, plus roughly \$1.7M in lost corporate deductions. A Company non-renewal at the end of the term would trigger \$3,532,875 of severance that the Term Sheet does not provide at all. Single-trigger vesting would release \$5.2M of unvested equity at a Change in Control even if she stays employed.

**Three priority flags.**

\(A\) Section 409A. The draft has no 409A provision at all: no savings clause, no six-month specified-employee delay, no separate-payment designation, and a Good Reason definition outside the involuntary-separation safe harbor. Its 75-day bonus window falls one day outside the short-term deferral period for FY2026. We add a full Section 17 and convert non-CIC severance to 18-month installments. (B) Dodd-Frank clawback. The draft contains no acknowledgment of the Rule 10D-1 Clawback Policy, which NYSE Section 303A.14 requires, and its bespoke indemnity could be read to cover clawed-back pay, which is prohibited. We add Section 18 using the Ashford & Sterling prescribed language. (C) Meridian non-compete. The January 6, 2026 start date falls 68 days before the Meridian covenant expires on March 15, 2026. The draft documents Pinnacle's knowledge of the covenant and shifts the compliance burden onto the Company, and the expiry date does not reconcile with her still being employed at Meridian. We need the Meridian agreement before signing. Our redline adds full representations and warranties, a right to defer the start date, and a no-Good-Reason carve-out for transition restrictions.

**Other must-fix structural issues.**

Governance: a Board nomination covenant and a minimum of eight direct reports, both wired into Good Reason. Termination architecture: a Cause definition limited to felony, embezzlement over \$10,000 and uncured breach, with a two-thirds Board vote and a good-faith defense; a seven-trigger Good Reason definition including a catch-all; no release; and Company non-renewal treated as termination without Cause. Restrictive covenants: a 6-month non-compete limited to household cleaning, a non-solicit covering direct reports only, no customer non-solicit, and unconditional garden leave at full salary. Disputes: Minnesota courts, Minnesota law (which under Minn. Stat. Section 181.988 would likely void the non-compete outright) and one-way fee shifting. Missing protections: no inventions assignment, no Section 409A provision and no clawback acknowledgment.

**Recommended approach.**

Return a full counter-draft conformed to the Term Sheet, using the redline language in Part V, with a short transmittal to Hu & Calloway. Neither the transmittal nor the margin comments may mention the Playbook. They should describe positions as "the Company's standard for executive officers" or "the approved compensation package." The margin comments in this document are drafted to that standard and can be carried into the counter-draft as they are. We have built in a small set of cost-neutral concessions (Part VI) to signal good faith without moving economics. The negotiation narrative is strong: the approved package already exceeds her Meridian package, with base +12.0% and target cash +8.9%, a \$500,000 signing bonus, and a \$3.2M make-whole that replaces her forfeited equity dollar for dollar.

## Headline Economics at a Glance

1252:### Issue 40 --- Cash severance 24 months base + 2x target, lump sum within 30 days (vs. 18 months + 1x target, installments)
### Issue 40 --- Cash severance 24 months base + 2x target, lump sum within 30 days (vs. 18 months + 1x target, installments)

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Draft § 10.1(i)**   **Severity: Critical**   **Category: Must-Reject**   Impact: \$2,775,000 vs. \$1,575,000 = +\$1,200,000 (+76.2%) at initial rates. Year-3 draft rates: \$3,059,437.50 (+\$1,484,437.50)
  --------------------- ------------------------ --------------------------- ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Draft provision:** Lump sum of 24 months of base plus 2x target within 30 days (\$750,000 x 2 + \$637,500 x 2 = \$2,775,000), at then-current (escalated) rates.

**Approved baseline:** Term Sheet Section 8: 18 months of base (\$1,050,000) plus 1x target (\$525,000) = \$1,575,000, paid in substantially equal installments over 18 months starting on the first payroll date after day 60, with catch-up. Playbook Sections VI.A/B and Appendix B: installments are mandatory, and 24 months plus 2x is the CEO formula.

**Analysis:** The draft gives the COO the CEO's severance formula. I've produced `redline-markup-commentary.docx`. It opens cleanly (parsed back with parse-doc), passes `validate.py`, and is the only file in /workspace/output.

**Main finding:** the Hu & Calloway draft cannot be signed in its current form. I found 70 deviations from the approved term sheet and the playbook: 19 Critical, 19 High, 17 Medium and 15 Low. 59 are must-reject; 11 are negotiable, each with stated limits.

**What the draft would cost compared with the term sheet:**
- **Year-1 target pay:** base + target bonus + annual equity rises from $2,725,000 to $3,387,500 (+$662,500, +24.3%).
- **Three-year term, recurring:** +$2,300,685.53 at target, or +$3,526,500.17 at maximum bonus. A further $637,500 of bonus is guaranteed for FY2026–FY2027 regardless of performance.
- **Termination without Cause in year 1:** about +$5.29M.
- **Change in control plus termination:** about +$5.94M, including an estimated ~$2.85M excise-tax gross-up, plus roughly $1.7M in lost corporate deductions.
- **Company non-renewal at end of term:** about +$3.53M, where the term sheet pays nothing.
- **Single-trigger vesting:** $5.2M of equity would vest at a change in control even if she stays.
- **Severance and change-in-control cash:** +$1.2M and +$1.7M respectively.

Several of these figures rest on my own assumptions, all listed in the Appendix. The COBRA premium ($2,500/month), the gross-up estimate and the travel/perk figures are illustrative and need confirming by Kendra and the Company's tax advisers.

**The three flagged issues:**
- **409A:** the draft has no savings clause, no six-month specified-employee delay, a Good Reason definition outside the 409A safe harbor, and a 75-day bonus window that lands on March 16, 2027, one day past the short-term deferral cutoff.
  - A 30-day lump sum after an involuntary termination is generally exempt from 409A. The real defects are the Good Reason definition and the missing delay.
  - I added a full new Section 17 and converted non-change-in-control severance to 18-month installments.
- **Dodd-Frank clawback:** the acknowledgment is missing, and the draft's indemnity could be read to cover clawed-back pay, which the SEC rule prohibits. I added a new Section 18 using Ashford & Sterling's prescribed language.
- **Meridian non-compete:** the January 6 start falls 68 days before the covenant expires on March 15, 2026. The expiry date also doesn't fit with her still working at Meridian; if it actually runs from her future departure, the overlap could be close to a year.
  - The term sheet says we have already reviewed the Meridian agreement, but Elise's email asks us to get it. We have no copy.
  - Minnesota's 2023 non-compete ban (Minn. Stat. §181.988) may matter depending on when she signed it.
  - The redline adds her representations and warranties, a Company right to push the start to March 16, 2026, and a rule that restricting her duties during the overlap is not Good Reason.

**Other findings worth knowing:**
- The draft's Minnesota choice of law would likely void Pinnacle's own non-compete under that same statute.
- The garden-leave clause literally pays a second full salary during employment.
- The customer non-solicit was dropped: the numbering jumps from 12(b) to 12(d).
- There is no inventions-assignment clause despite the section heading.
- The source documents disagree with each other on the clawback policy's name (three versions), the equity plan's name, and whether time-based RSUs are clawback-covered.
- The playbook has two errors: it cites $220K instead of $230K as the 2025 key-employee threshold, and it says North Carolina has no inventions statute when N.C. Gen. Stat. §66-57.1 exists.
- Opposing counsel is "Margaret Hsu" in the email but "Margaret Hu" in the draft's notice block.

**How the document is built:**
- A summary table of all 70 issues sits at the top (issue, section, severity, category, dollar impact), followed by an exposure analysis, the three flags, section-by-section analysis with redline language, a must-reject vs. negotiable map, a discrepancies and action-items list, and the calculation assumptions.
- The redlines are real Word tracked changes, with a plain-text deletion/insertion line under each so they still read without Track Changes on.
- Each of the 70 issues carries a Word margin comment written so it can go to Hu & Calloway as-is: none mentions the playbook or the internal term sheet.

Files are in /workspace/output:
- redline-markup-commentary.docx
